definition_zh: v. 赞扬；推荐；托付
definition_en: to praise someone formally, or to recommend them
core_image: 经理在会议上当众表扬一名新员工
scene: 经理当众表扬了这位新员工，说她做事可靠。 The manager commended the new employee for her reliability.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：commend 指赞扬；句意是经理当众表扬了这位新员工，说她做事可靠。

pos.zh: 赞扬；推荐；托付

senses.title: To praise formally
senses.definition: to praise someone officially or publicly
senses.definitionCN: 正式或公开地称赞某人
senses.example: The judge commended the witness for her honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 法官称赞证人的诚实。
senses.why: Latin commendare joins com, fully, with mandare, to entrust.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 commendare 由 com（完全）与 mandare（托付）合成。

senses.title: To recommend or entrust
senses.definition: to hand something over to someone for safekeeping, or suggest it
senses.definitionCN: 把东西交给某人保管，或加以推荐
senses.example: I commend this book to anyone who loves history.
senses.exampleCN: 我把这本书推荐给所有爱历史的人。
senses.why: The older sense of entrusting survives in formal English.
senses.whyCN: 「托付」这一旧义仍见于正式英语。

intro.en: Commend joins a prefix meaning fully to a verb meaning entrust.
intro.cn: commend 把表示「完全」的前缀与表示「托付」的动词连在一起。

items.en: Mandare means to entrust or order.
items.cn: mandare 意为托付或命令。

items.en: Commendare means to entrust fully.
items.cn: commendare 意为完全托付。

items.en: French comander softened the spelling.
items.cn: 法语 comander 改变了拼写。

items.en: Commend came to mean praise.
items.cn: 十四世纪 commend 获得「称赞」义。

items.en: Reports still commend staff for good work.
items.cn: 现代报告仍用 commend 表扬员工。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the comm- opening; the near-meaning group names praise and recommendation.
note.cn: 形近组共享 comm- 开头；近义组列出称赞与推荐。

entries.definition: A spoken or written remark.
entries.definitionCN: 评论。

entries.definition: To begin.
entries.definitionCN: 开始。

entries.definition: To order or control.
entries.definitionCN: 命令；指挥。

entries.definition: To say good things about.
entries.definitionCN: 赞扬。

entries.definition: To clap or approve openly.
entries.definitionCN: 鼓掌；赞许。

entries.definition: To suggest as good.
entries.definitionCN: 推荐。

normal.en: To commend is to praise openly.

normal.en: You can commend a book too.

abstract.en: A book passed to a friend.

examples.cn: 报告赞扬团队的迅速。

examples.en: She was highly commended in the competition.
examples.cn: 她在比赛中获高度赞扬。

examples.en: I commend this novel to every reader.
examples.cn: 我把这部小说推荐给每位读者。

definition_zh: 指责的；非难的；控诉的；问罪式的
definition_en: suggesting that someone has done something wrong, or expressing an accusation
core_image: 皱起的眉头直指对方，像一根手指点在人身上
scene: 他翻出账本逐条核对，脸色越来越沉，抬头时满屋都静了。 He gave her an accusatory look when the money was found missing.
sceneCN: 这里 accusatory 是「指责的、非难的」（第 1 个义项：用目光或语气暗示某人做错了事）；句意是发现钱不见了，他向她投去问罪的一瞥。

pos.zh: 指责的；非难的；控诉的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「指责地；非难地」
同根名词，义为「指控；指责」
同根动词，义为「指控；指责」

senses.title: Blaming with looks or words
senses.definition: showing by a look, tone, or remark that you think someone has done something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 用眼神、语气或话语表明你认为某人做错了事
senses.example: She shot him an accusatory glance across the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她隔着桌子朝他投去责备的一瞥。
senses.why: The Latin causa, a legal case, gives accuse its sense of naming a fault; the adjective keeps that pointing gesture on the face and in the voice.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 causa（案件）给了 accuse「指出过错」的含义；形容词把这种指认的姿势保留在脸上和语气里。

senses.title: Formally charging in law
senses.definition: relating to a formal statement that someone has committed a crime
senses.definitionCN: 与指控某人犯罪的正式陈述有关的
senses.example: The lawyer reviewed the accusatory documents before the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 开庭前律师审阅了控诉文书。
senses.why: The courtroom is where naming a fault becomes official; the adjective moves from a glance to the formal papers of a charge.
senses.whyCN: 法庭是指认过错变成正式手续的地方；这个形容词从一瞥移向正式的指控文书。

intro.en: The word belongs to the Latin family of calling someone to answer a charge.
intro.cn: 这个词属于拉丁语中「传唤某人应诉」的词族。

items.en: causa meant a legal case, a reason, or a matter brought before a judge.
items.cn: 拉丁语 causa 指案件、缘由，或提交法官审理的事由。

items.en: accusare joined ad-, towards, with causari, to give as a cause or charge.
items.cn: accusare 由表示「朝向」的 ad- 与 causari（提出事由）结合而成。

items.en: acuser carried the legal charge into Romance speech.
items.cn: 古法语 acuser 把法律指控义带进了罗曼语。

items.en: accuse and accusation entered English through Anglo-French legal use.
items.cn: accuse 与 accusation 经盎格鲁-法语的法律用语进入英语。

items.en: accusatory now describes the blaming tone of a look or a question as much as a formal charge.
items.cn: 如今 accusatory 既形容正式指控，也形容目光或问句里的责备意味。

note.en: The first group is the causa family; the second gathers words for blame with different weights.
note.cn: 第一组是 causa 词族；第二组收集轻重不同的指责类词。

definition_zh: 气候学；研究气候的形成、分布、变化及其影响的学科
definition_en: the scientific study of climates: how they form, vary over time and space, and affect living things
core_image: 一整面墙的等温线地图，红线与蓝线像经纬一样把大陆切成许多带
scene: 大学的教室里，学生把一组全球温度曲线叠在同一张图上。 Modern climatology relies on satellite data as well as long station records.
sceneCN: 这里 climatology 指「研究气候的学科」（第 1 个义项：气候学总称）；句意为现代气候学既依赖卫星数据，也依赖长期台站记录。图中可辨识物件：等温线地图、曲线图、卫星轨迹、观测台站。

pos.zh: 气候学（不可数名词，指学科）
某地的气候志；气候平均状况（可数用法）

forms.label: 复数（不同地区的气候志）

senses.title: The discipline
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies climates as long-term systems
senses.definitionCN: 把气候当作长期系统来研究的科学分支
senses.example: Climatology asks why two regions at the same latitude differ.
senses.exampleCN: 气候学追问：为何同纬度的两个地区气候不同。
senses.why: the suffix for 'study' attached to climate names the discipline as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 表示「研究」的后缀加在 climate 上，指的就是这门学科整体。

senses.title: Physical climatology
senses.definition: the branch that explains climate through radiation, heat, moisture and circulation
senses.definitionCN: 用辐射、热量、水汽与环流来解释气候的分支
senses.example: Physical climatology models how the ocean stores heat.
senses.exampleCN: 物理气候学研究海洋如何储存热量。
senses.why: physics supplies the mechanisms, so the discipline splits off a branch named for them.
senses.whyCN: 物理学提供机制，于是学科分出以它命名的一支。

senses.title: Regional climatology
senses.definition: the branch that describes and compares the climates of particular regions
senses.definitionCN: 描述并比较特定地区气候的分支
senses.example: Regional climatology maps the monsoon belt in detail.
senses.exampleCN: 区域气候学详细绘制季风带。
senses.why: a region is the natural unit of description, so the field grew a branch named for it.
senses.whyCN: 地区是描述气候的自然单位，于是学科长出一支以它命名的分枝。

senses.title: Historical climatology
senses.titleCN: 古气候学与历史气候学
senses.definition: the branch that reconstructs past climates from ice, sediment, tree rings and written records
senses.definitionCN: 从冰芯、沉积、年轮与文献重建过去气候的分支
senses.example: Historical climatology reads old harvest logs for frost dates.
senses.exampleCN: 历史气候学从旧收成记录里读出霜期。
senses.why: a climate has a history, so the discipline grew a branch that looks backward.
senses.whyCN: 气候有自己的历史，于是学科长出一支回望过去的枝。

senses.title: Applied climatology
senses.definition: the use of climate knowledge in farming, building, health and energy planning
senses.definitionCN: 把气候知识用于农业、建筑、健康与能源规划
senses.example: Applied climatology advises growers on planting dates.
senses.exampleCN: 应用气候学为种植者提供播期建议。
senses.why: users needed answers rather than descriptions, so a branch was named for its use.
senses.whyCN: 使用者要的是答案而非描述，于是出现一支以用途命名的分枝。

senses.title: Statistical climatology and modelling
senses.titleCN: 统计气候学与气候建模
senses.definition: the branch that summarises climate statistically and simulates it with computers
senses.definitionCN: 用统计方法概括气候并用计算机模拟的分支
senses.example: Statistical climatology separates a trend from ordinary noise.
senses.exampleCN: 统计气候学把趋势与普通噪声分开。
senses.why: climate is a distribution rather than a single event, so numerical summary became a branch of its own.
senses.whyCN: 气候是一个分布而非单次事件，于是数值概括自成一门分枝。

senses.title: The climatology of a place
senses.definition: a counted noun: the documented climate of one place, often as a long series of averages
senses.definitionCN: 可数用法：某一个地方有记录的气候，常表现为一长串平均值
senses.example: The station published a climatology of the upper valley.
senses.exampleCN: 该站发布了上游山谷的气候志。
senses.why: one place's full file of averages is a countable product, so the discipline name gained a countable use.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方整套的平均记录是可数的成果，于是学科名多出一个可数用法。

senses.title: A long-term average state
senses.definition: technical: the average condition used as a baseline in forecasting and modelling
senses.definitionCN: 技术用法：预报与建模中作为基准的长期平均状况
senses.example: Models compare each season with the modelled climatology.
senses.exampleCN: 模式把每个季节与模式算出的气候平均态作比较。
senses.why: forecasting needs a baseline, and the discipline's name became the word for that baseline.
senses.whyCN: 预报需要一个基准，于是学科之名变成了这个基准的叫法。

intro.en: Climatology joins climate with the Greek-derived suffix -logy 'study'. The word belongs to the scientific vocabulary of the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: climatology 由 climate 与希腊来源的后缀 -logy「研究」组合而成，属于十九世纪的科学词汇。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek klima 'slope, zone' named the belts of the earth fixed by latitude; it comes from klimein 'to lean'.
items.cn: 希腊 klima「斜坡、地带」指由纬度确定的地球条带，出自 klimein「倾斜」。

items.en: Greek -logia 'account, study' comes from logos 'word, reason, account'; Latin -logia passed it into the learned languages of Europe.
items.cn: 希腊 -logia「记述、研究」出自 logos「言词、理性、说明」；拉丁 -logia 把它传入欧洲的学术语言。

items.en: English climate arrived in the late fourteenth century from Old French and Latin, first as a geographical belt and later as a region's weather.
items.cn: 英语 climate 在十四世纪末经古法语与拉丁语进入，先指地理上的带，后指一个地区的天气。

items.en: Climatology appears in the nineteenth century as the name for the systematic study of climates, beside the older descriptive term climatography.
items.cn: climatology 在十九世纪出现，成为系统研究气候的学科名，与较早的描述性术语 climatography 并存。

items.en: In the twentieth century the field split into physical, regional, statistical and historical branches, and the word came to cover computer modelling as well.
items.cn: 二十世纪这门学科分成物理、区域、统计与历史等分支，这个词也开始涵盖计算机建模。

items.en: First English date approximate: no exact first citation is agreed, and the term is usually dated to the early nineteenth century. Its formation, climate plus the suffix for 'study', is transparent.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：没有公认的确切首见书证，这个词通常被定在十九世纪初。它的构成——climate 加表示「研究」的后缀——则一目了然。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike names from neighbouring fields and subfields; group two holds the wider or narrower sciences that are often confused with climatology.
note.cn: 第一组是邻近领域与分支中形似的名称；第二组是常与气候学混淆的、范围更宽或更窄的学科。

entries.definition: The descriptive mapping and tabulation of climates; -graphy means writing or drawing, while -logy means reasoned study.
entries.definitionCN: 对气候的描述性制图与制表；-graphy 意为书写描绘，-logy 意为有理据的研究。

entries.definition: The reconstruction of ancient climates; it is a branch of climatology, not a rival term.
entries.definitionCN: 对古代气候的重建；它是气候学的分支，而非对立名称。

entries.definition: The study of climate as it affects living things; again a branch built with a prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 研究气候对生物影响的学科；同样是以前缀构成的分支。

entries.definition: The adjective of climatology; it describes data or averages rather than the discipline itself.
entries.definitionCN: climatology 的形容词，描述数据或平均值，而非学科本身。

entries.definition: The science of the atmosphere and of weather over short periods; climatology studies the long average of that weather.
entries.definitionCN: 研究大气与短期天气的科学；气候学研究这些天气的长期平均。

entries.definition: The everyday and policy name for the same field, often used where climatology sounds academic.
entries.definitionCN: 同一领域的日常与政策名称，常在气候学听起来太学术的场合使用。

entries.definition: The broad study of the atmosphere, of which climatology is one part.
entries.definitionCN: 对大气层的广泛研究，气候学只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: The study of the earth's surface and its places; climate is only one of its subjects.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地球表面及其地方的综合学科；气候只是其主题之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: climate plus -logy, the suffix for a reasoned study.
normal.cn: climate 加 -logy，即表示有理据研究的后缀。

normal.en: The family runs climatology, climatologist, climatological, paleoclimatology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 climatology、climatologist、climatological、paleoclimatology。

normal.en: The oldest sister term is climatography, which describes rather than explains.
normal.cn: 最早的姊妹术语是 climatography，它描述而不解释。

normal.en: The discipline is counted in decades and centuries, unlike meteorology.
normal.cn: 这门学科以十年与百年为尺度，与气象学不同。

normal.en: Branches are marked by prefixes: physical, regional, historical, applied, statistical.
normal.cn: 分支由前缀标出：物理、区域、历史、应用、统计。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of isotherms cutting a continent into belts.
abstract.cn: 想象一墙等温线把大陆切成条带。

abstract.en: Picture a single average drawn through a century of storms.
abstract.cn: 想象一条平均值穿过一个世纪的风暴。

abstract.en: Picture a library where every drawer holds one year of weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每个抽屉装着一年的天气。

examples.en: Climatology explains why the two coasts differ despite equal latitude.
examples.cn: 气候学解释了为何两片海岸纬度相同却气候不同。

examples.en: She studied climatology before moving into policy.
examples.cn: 她在进入政策领域之前学的是气候学。

examples.en: The paper compares observed rainfall with the model climatology.
examples.cn: 这篇论文把观测降水与模式的气候平均态作比较。

dict_mnemonic.text: climate 是气候，-logy 是「学科」：研究气候的学问就是气候学；记住它研究的是几十年的平均，而不是明天下不下雨

root: 希腊 klima「斜坡、地带」→ 拉丁 clima → 英语 climate；再加希腊 -logia「研究」→ climatology；与 meteorology（气象学）分工不同。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one science outward: the discipline itself, then its physical, regional, historical, applied and statistical branches, then a place's documented climate, and finally the average used as a baseline.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一门学科向外铺开：先是学科本身，再是物理、区域、历史、应用与统计各分支，然后是一个地方有记录的气候，最后是作为基准的平均态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall of isotherms cutting a continent into belts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一墙等温线把大陆切成一条条带。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: the suffix for study turns climate into a discipline.
branches.cn: 整体：表示研究的后缀把气候变成一门学科。

branches.en: PHYSICS: radiation, heat and circulation explain the pattern.
branches.cn: 物理：辐射、热量与环流解释这种模式。

branches.en: SPACE AND TIME: one branch compares regions, another reconstructs past climates.
branches.cn: 空间与时间：一支比较地区，一支重建过去的气候。

branches.en: USE AND NUMBER: knowledge is applied to farming and building, and summarised by statistics and models.
branches.cn: 应用与数字：知识被用于农业与建筑，又被统计与模式概括。

branches.en: THE LOCAL RECORD AND THE BASELINE: a place's counted climate, and the average a forecast measures against.
branches.cn: 地方记录与基准：一个地方可数的气候，以及预报用来对照的平均值。

intro.en: Climatology is a compound of a noun and a suffix of Greek origin, and each half has its own family of English words.
intro.cn: climatology 由一个名词与一个希腊来源的后缀复合而成，两半各自都有英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek klima and Latin clima give climate; Greek -logia and Latin -logia give the second half, which also builds biology, geology and meteorology.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 klima 与拉丁 clima 给出 climate；希腊 -logia 与拉丁 -logia 给出后半，也构成 biology、geology、meteorology 等词。

items.example: The word described a tilt before it described a region.
items.exampleCN: 这个词先描述倾斜，后描述地区。

items.example: The suffix names a field of knowledge.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀为一片知识领域命名。

items.meaning: the long-term weather of a region
items.example: The climate of the plateau is severe.
Climatology compares centuries of records.
items.exampleCN: 气候学比较数百年的记录。

items.example: A climatologist joined the field team.
items.exampleCN: 一位气候学家加入了野外队伍。

items.example: The climatological average hides the storm.
items.exampleCN: 气候平均值掩盖了那场风暴。

items.example: Paleoclimatology reads ice cores.
Bioclimatology maps mosquito ranges.
items.exampleCN: 生物气候学绘制蚊虫分布范围。

items.example: Meteorology forecast the storm; climatology counted it.
items.exampleCN: 气象学预报了风暴，气候学把它计入统计。

definition_zh: 碱；（化学）强碱；碱性物质
definition_en: a substance that reacts with acids to form salts, turning litmus blue
core_image: 一杯滑腻的碱水遇到酸便 fizz 着握手言和
scene: 实验室里，蓝色石蕊纸浸进烧杯立刻显出深蓝。 The chemist neutralized the acid with a mild alkali.
sceneCN: 这里 alkali 是「碱」（第 1 个义项：与酸反应成盐的化学物质）；句意是化学家用温和的碱中和了酸。

pos.zh: 碱；强碱
碱性的

alkali 加 -oid，义为「生物碱」（如咖啡因）

senses.title: A substance neutralizing acids
senses.definition: a chemical substance that turns litmus blue and neutralizes acids to form salts
senses.definitionCN: 使石蕊变蓝、与酸中和成盐的化学物质
senses.example: Add a little alkali to soften the hard water.
senses.exampleCN: 加一点碱来软化硬水。
senses.why: The Arabic word named the burnt ashes of plants from which the substance was first obtained.
senses.whyCN: 阿拉伯语原词指焚烧植物所得的灰烬，这种物质最初正是从灰中提取的。

senses.title: Alkaline quality or soil
senses.definition: the alkaline character of a solution or land, or such soil itself
senses.definitionCN: 溶液或土地的碱性特征，或这类土壤本身
senses.example: Farmers fought the alkali that whitened their fields.
senses.exampleCN: 农民们与使田地泛白的碱化作斗争。
senses.why: When the white crust on arid land is made of these salts, the substance's name passes to the land itself.
senses.whyCN: 干旱土地上泛白的盐霜正是这类盐分，物质之名便转指土地本身。

intro.en: From Arabic for 'the ashes', carried through medieval Latin into European chemistry.
intro.cn: 源自阿拉伯语「灰烬」，经中世纪拉丁语进入欧洲化学。

items.en: al-qily meant the ashes of the saltwort plant, with the article al- attached.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语 al-qily 指滨藜属植物的灰烬，al- 为定冠词。

items.en: Latin alcali or alkali named the same calcined ashes used in glassmaking.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 alcali 指同样的、用于制玻璃的煅烧灰烬。

items.en: Old French alcali passed the word on to English alchemists.
items.cn: 古法语 alcali 把该词传给英语的炼金术士。

items.en: English alkali first meant the ashes and their caustic salts.
items.cn: 14 世纪英语 alkali 最初指灰烬及其苛性盐类。

items.en: Modern chemistry redefined it as bases that neutralize acids; alkali metals, alkaline batteries follow.
items.cn: 现代化学将其定义为中和酸类的碱；碱金属、碱性电池等术语由此派生。

note.en: The first group gathers the Arabic al- family and a look-alike; the second gathers words for bases and salts.
note.cn: 第一组收阿拉伯语 al- 词族与一个形近词；第二组收「碱」与「盐」相关词。

entries.definition: a plant substance like an alkali, such as caffeine

entries.definition: to make or become alkaline

entries.definition: a strongly burning alkali such as caustic soda
entries.definitionCN: 苛性物质（如烧碱）

entries.definition: a strong alkaline solution, especially of sodium hydroxide
entries.definitionCN: 碱液（尤指氢氧化钠溶液）

entries.definition: a salt of carbonic acid, often alkaline

normal.en: Alkali turns litmus paper blue; acid turns it red.

normal.en: Al- words from Arabic: alkali, alcohol, algebra.

normal.en: alkaline is the adjective; alkaline batteries use it.

abstract.en: See a strip of litmus paper turning deep blue in a beaker.

abstract.en: Imagine a white crust creeping across an irrigated field.

examples.en: Soap is made by boiling fat with an alkali.

examples.cn: 湖水碱性太强，多数鱼类无法生存。

examples.en: Sodium is the classic alkali metal.

sensesIntro.en: Two senses spread from the same white powder: the chemical base itself, then the alkaline land it coats.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项由同一把白色粉末展开：先是作为化学碱本身，再是被它覆盖的碱性土地。

definition_zh: 散布；扩散；分散；传播
definition_en: the act or process of spreading things out over a wider area, or the state of being scattered in different directions
core_image: 蒲公英种子被风一吹，从一处散向整片河谷
scene: 秋天，蒲公英的种子被一阵风带离母株，散落到河谷各处。 In autumn, dandelion seeds are carried away from the parent plant by a gust of wind and undergo wide dispersal across the river valley.
sceneCN: 这里 dispersal 是「散布、扩散」（第 2 个义项：生物繁殖体的传播）；句意：秋天，蒲公英种子被一阵风吹离母株，散布到河谷各处。

pos.zh: 散布；扩散；分散（多作不可数；指一次具体扩散过程时可数）

derivatives.zh: 可分散的；可溶解分散的

senses.title: Scatter outward from one point
senses.definition: the process by which things that were gathered in one place move apart and cover a wider area
senses.definitionCN: 原本聚在一处的东西分开移动、覆盖更大范围的过程
senses.example: The dispersal of the swarm began when the queen left the hive.
senses.exampleCN: 蜂群随着蜂王离巢而开始散开。
senses.why: Latin dispergere joins dis- 'apart' to spargere 'to strew, scatter'. The prefix does the work of separation, so the noun names the outward breaking-up of a group.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dispergere 把 dis-「分开」与 spargere「撒、铺散」结合；前缀本身承担“分离”的动作，因此这个名词指群体向外散开的过程。

senses.title: Biological seed or spore spread
senses.definition: the movement of seeds, spores, or larvae away from the parent organism to new places
senses.definitionCN: 种子、孢子或幼体离开亲本、到达新地点的过程
senses.example: Wind dispersal lets maple seeds colonize clearings far from the parent tree.
senses.exampleCN: 风力传播让枫树种子在远离母树的空地上定殖。
senses.why: Once spargere is applied to living propagules, the 'strewing' becomes sowing: the plant scatters its seeds exactly as a hand scatters grain, and the distance travelled is what the term measures.
senses.whyCN: 当 spargere 用于活体繁殖体时，“撒开”就变成了“播种”：植物像手撒谷粒一样把种子撒出去，而这个词度量的正是种子移动的距离。

senses.title: Population dispersal: individuals leave a group
senses.titleCN: 种群扩散：个体迁出群体
senses.definition: the movement of individuals away from a crowded or natal population into new areas
senses.definitionCN: 个体离开拥挤的或出生的种群、进入新区域的移动
senses.example: Dispersal reduces competition because young animals leave the densest ranges.
senses.exampleCN: 扩散能减轻竞争，因为幼兽会离开最密集的活动范围。
senses.why: The same outward scatter is read as a demographic event: what moves is not grain but individual animals, and the result is a new distribution of the species.
senses.whyCN: 同一种向外散开被读作种群事件：移动的不是谷粒而是动物个体，结果是该物种形成新的分布。

senses.title: Physical or chemical dispersion
senses.titleCN: 物理化学意义上的分散
senses.definition: the spreading of particles, molecules, or droplets through a medium so that they are no longer clumped
senses.definitionCN: 颗粒、分子或液滴在介质中铺开而不再聚集
senses.example: Ulasonic stirring produces a fine dispersal of clay particles in water.
senses.exampleCN: 超声搅拌使黏土颗粒在水中形成细微分散。
senses.why: In the laboratory the Latin image becomes literal: spargere describes particles strewn through a liquid, and the noun names the resulting non-clumped state.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，这个拉丁意象变成字面意义：spargere 描述颗粒被撒进液体，名词则指由此得到的非聚集状态。

senses.title: Dispersal of a crowd or gathering
senses.definition: the breaking up of an assembled crowd, often because it is told or forced to leave
senses.definitionCN: 聚集人群的解散，常因被要求或被强制离开
senses.example: The dispersal of the crowd took less than ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 人群的散开不到十分钟就完成了。
senses.why: A crowd is a gathering held in one place; dis- pulls it apart in all directions, so the nominal form describes the moment the assembly stops being an assembly.
senses.whyCN: 人群是聚集在一处的集合；dis- 把它向四面八方拉开，因此名词形式描述集会不再成为集会的那个时刻。

senses.title: Spread of information or ideas
senses.definition: the spreading of knowledge, news, or beliefs to many people or places
senses.definitionCN: 知识、消息或观念传播到许多人或许多地方
senses.example: Printing enabled the rapid dispersal of scientific ideas across Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷术使科学观念在欧洲迅速传播。
senses.why: The metaphor extends from physical scattering to information: ideas leave one mind and are strewn among many, and the word keeps the same outward direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻从物理撒散延伸到信息：观念离开一个头脑、撒布到许多人之间，词义保持同样的向外方向。

senses.title: Decentralization of power or resources
senses.definition: the distribution of authority, money, or functions away from a single center
senses.definitionCN: 权力、资金或职能从单一中心向外分配
senses.example: The dispersal of authority to regional offices weakened the capital's control.
senses.exampleCN: 把权力下放到地区办事处削弱了首都的控制。
senses.why: Here what was held at one center is scattered to several points. The Latin separation is political rather than physical, but the shape of the movement is identical.
senses.whyCN: 这里原本集中在一处的东西被散到若干点。拉丁语中的“分离”是政治性的而非物理性的，但移动的形状完全相同。

senses.title: Forced scattering: police dispersal
senses.definition: the clearing of a crowd or gathering by authorities, sometimes with force
senses.definitionCN: 当局对人群或集会的清场，有时使用武力
senses.example: The police ordered the dispersal of the illegal demonstration.
senses.exampleCN: 警方下令驱散这次非法示威。
senses.why: When an authority does the scattering, the neutral 'spreading out' acquires a coercive edge; dis- is imposed on the crowd from outside rather than happening by itself.
senses.whyCN: 当驱散由当局执行时，中性的“散开”带上了强制色彩；dis- 是从外部强加于人群，而不是人群自行散开。

intro.en: Dispersal is a nineteenth-century noun built on the older verb disperse, which came through French from Latin dispergere. The date is approximate; the underlying PIE root is a reconstruction.
intro.cn: dispersal 是 19 世纪在较早的动词 disperse 基础上构成的名词；disperse 经由法语来自拉丁语 dispergere。年代为大致估计，最底层原始印欧词根属于重构。

items.en: The noun dispersal is recorded from the 1820s in the sense 'act of dispersing', formed by adding the native suffix -al to the verb disperse.
items.cn: 名词 dispersal 于 19 世纪 20 年代被记录，义为“分散的行为”，由动词 disperse 加本族后缀 -al 构成。

items.en: The verb goes back to Latin dispersus, past participle of dispergere 'to scatter, disperse'.
items.cn: 该动词可追溯到拉丁语 dispersus，即 dispergere「撒开、分散」的过去分词。

items.en: dispergere = dis- 'apart, in different directions' + spargere 'to strew, sprinkle, scatter'. The same spargere gives sparse, intersperse and aspersion.
items.cn: dispergere = dis-「分开、向不同方向」+ spargere「撒、洒、散布」。同一个 spargere 还产生 sparse、intersperse、aspersion。

items.en: Spargere is traced to a reconstructed root *sper- 'to strew', also seen in Greek speirein 'to sow' and sperma 'seed'. The reconstruction is conventional rather than directly attested, so the deepest layer is source uncertain.
items.cn: spargere 被追溯到重构词根 *sper-「撒播」，同样见于希腊语 speirein「播种」与 sperma「种子」。这一重构是通行做法而非直接证据，故最深层来源不确定。

items.en: Old French disperser and its participle gave English the verb in the 14th century; English later coined the noun rather than borrowing a Latin noun.
items.cn: 古法语 disperser 及其分词在 14 世纪把该动词带入英语；英语后来是自己造出名词，而不是借入拉丁名词。

items.en: Modern English keeps two nouns: dispersal for the process, especially in biology and planning, and dispersion for physical scattering such as light dispersion.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两个名词：dispersal 指过程，尤其在生物学与规划领域；dispersion 指物理上的分散，如光的色散。

note.cn: 第一组区分拼写相近的词，第二组比较意思接近的词。先看词形，再看词义。

entries.definition: the physical scattering of light or particles; also a statistical spread. It is the Latin-derived sibling of dispersal.
entries.definitionCN: 光或粒子的物理分散；也指统计离差。它是 dispersal 的拉丁式同源名词。

entries.definition: the act of getting rid of something, from dispose (dis- + ponere 'to place'). It has nothing to do with scattering.
entries.definitionCN: 处理、处置的行为，来自 dispose（dis- + ponere「放置」）。与“撒散”无关。

entries.definition: thinly spread; not dense. It descends from Latin sparsus, the participle of the same spargere.
entries.definitionCN: 稀疏的；不密集的。它来自拉丁语 sparsus，即同一个 spargere 的分词。

entries.definition: a substance that keeps particles apart in a liquid; a product noun from disperse.
entries.definitionCN: 使颗粒在液体中保持分离的物质；由 disperse 构成的产品名词。

entries.definition: the action of throwing things in many directions. It is plainer and more physical than dispersal.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西向多方向抛散的动作。比 dispersal 更朴素、更偏物理。

entries.definition: the slow spreading of particles, heat, or ideas through a medium. It stresses gradual mixing rather than an initial scatter.
entries.definitionCN: 粒子、热量或观念在介质中的缓慢铺开。强调逐渐混合，而非最初的散开。

entries.definition: the act of extending over a wider area. It is the neutral everyday word that dispersal formalizes.
entries.definitionCN: 扩展到更广区域的行为。是 dispersal 所正式化的日常中性词。

entries.definition: the way things are placed or shared across an area or group. It names the result, while dispersal names the movement.
entries.definitionCN: 事物在某区域或群体中的放置或分配方式。它指结果，dispersal 指移动过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real phrases, and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实短语和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dis- means apart and spargere means to strew: dispersal is literally 'strewing apart'.
normal.cn: dis- 表示“分开”，spargere 表示“撒”：dispersal 字面就是“撒开”。

normal.en: Seed dispersal is the standard term in ecology for how plants move their seeds away from the parent.
normal.cn: seed dispersal 是生态学中表示植物把种子送离母株的标准术语。

normal.en: Dispersion is the physics cousin: light dispersion through a prism spreads colours apart.
normal.cn: dispersion 是物理学中的同源词：棱镜中的光色散把颜色分开。

normal.en: Sparse and intersperse share the same spargere root: sparse is 'scattered thin', intersperse is 'scatter between'.
normal.cn: sparse 与 intersperse 共享同一个 spargere 词根：sparse 是“撒得稀”，intersperse 是“撒在中间”。

normal.en: Police dispersal is the coercive branch: the crowd is scattered by order, not by wind.
normal.cn: police dispersal 是强制分支：人群是被命令驱散的，不是被风吹散的。

abstract.en: Picture one handful of grain released above a field: the hand opens, the grains separate in the air, and the pattern widens as they fall. That widening is dispersal.
abstract.cn: 想象一把谷粒在高处松开：手张开，谷粒在空中分离，落下时分布越来越宽。这个“变宽”就是 dispersal。

abstract.en: The same shape applies to seeds, animals, particles, ideas, and authority: something once held at one point is released to many points.
abstract.cn: 同一形状适用于种子、动物、颗粒、观念与权力：曾经集中在一点的东西被释放到许多点。

abstract.en: Dispersal is the movement, distribution is the final map; keeping the two apart prevents circular definitions.
abstract.cn: dispersal 是移动过程，distribution 是最终地图；把两者分开可以避免循环定义。

examples.en: The study tracked seed dispersal by attaching radio tags to wind-borne fruits.
examples.cn: 这项研究通过给风力传播的果实装上无线电标签来追踪种子扩散。

examples.en: Habitat loss blocks dispersal and leaves populations isolated in small patches.
examples.cn: 栖息地丧失阻断扩散，使种群被隔离在小块斑块中。

examples.en: The dispersal of the protest began only after the mayor's announcement.
examples.cn: 示威的驱散是在市长宣布之后才开始的。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地斯破手”——地上一撒，破开的手一扬，种子向四方散开 → dispersal 分散、传播

root: 拉丁语 dispergere「向不同方向撒开」，由 dis-（分开）+ spargere（撒、散布）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of dispersal, all one gesture: what was gathered at a point is released and widens outward, whether it is seeds, animals, particles, a crowd, news, or authority.
sensesIntro.cn: dispersal 的八个义项都源于同一个动作：原本集中在一点的东西被释放并向四周变宽——无论那是种子、动物、颗粒、人群、消息还是权力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand opens above a field and the grains separate as they fall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在田野上方张开，谷粒落下时彼此分开。

branches.en: SIMPLE SCATTER: objects or a crowd break apart in all directions.
branches.cn: 简单散开：物体或人群向四面八方分开。

branches.en: LIFE: seeds and animals leave the parent or natal group and reach new habitat.
branches.cn: 生命：种子和动物离开亲本或出生群，抵达新栖息地。

branches.en: MATTER: particles are strewn through a medium and stop clumping.
branches.cn: 物质：颗粒被撒入介质，不再聚集。

branches.en: ABSTRACT FLOW: ideas and authority move from one center to many points.
branches.cn: 抽象流动：观念与权力从单一中心流向多个点。

branches.en: FORCE: an authority imposes the scatter on a crowd from outside.
branches.cn: 强制：当局从外部把“散开”强加于人群。

intro.en: Dispersal is the verb disperse plus the noun suffix -al. Inside the verb, dis- is the only living prefix; spargere is a Latin verb stem, not a productive English element.
intro.cn: dispersal 是动词 disperse 加名词后缀 -al。动词内部只有 dis- 是仍可分析的活前缀；spargere 是拉丁动词词干，不是能产的英语成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin spargere 'to scatter' supplies sparse, aspersion and intersperse beside the dispergere family; the modern Greek seed words sperm and spermat- descend from a related but separate speirein.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spargere「撒」除了 dispergere 一族，还提供 sparse、aspersion、intersperse；现代希腊语系的 sperm、spermat- 则来自相关但另成一线的 speirein。

items.meaningCN: 分散的行为（-al 构成行为名词）
items.example: Seed dispersal is measured in metres.
items.exampleCN: 种子扩散以米为单位测量。

items.meaningCN: 向不同方向散开（dis- 分开 + spargere 撒）
items.example: The wind dispersed the smoke.

items.meaning: the state of being scattered; physical dispersion
items.meaningCN: 被分散的状态；物理色散（-ion 构成结果名词）
items.example: Dispersion of white light produces a spectrum.

items.meaningCN: 有分散倾向的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: Sandstone is a dispersive medium for water.
items.exampleCN: 砂岩对水是一种分散性介质。

items.meaning: able to be dispersed in a medium
items.meaningCN: 可分散于介质中的（-ible 表示“能够”）
items.example: The powder is dispersible in cold water.
items.exampleCN: 这种粉末可分散于冷水中。

items.example: Sparse grass covers the dry slope.
items.exampleCN: 稀疏的草覆盖着干旱的坡地。

items.meaningCN: 散布于其他事物之间（inter- 之间 + 撒）
items.example: Wildflowers were interspersed among the wheat.

items.meaning: a sprinkling, hence a slanderous remark
items.meaningCN: 洒水，引申为诽谤（-ion 名词）
items.example: He cast aspersions on the report.
items.exampleCN: 他对这份报告加以中伤。

definition_zh: 垄断性的；垄断的；具有垄断特征的
definition_en: relating to or resembling a monopoly; tending to exclude competition
core_image: 一张市场地图上，原本散布的许多小店被涂成同一种颜色，只剩一面招牌
scene: 监管人员把一张市场分布图铺在桌上，图上几乎所有街区都被涂成同一家公司的颜色。 Regulators accused the platform of monopolistic behaviour in the delivery market.
sceneCN: 这里 monopolistic 指「具有垄断特征的」（第 1 个义项：表现出单一卖方支配市场特征的）；句意为监管机构指控该平台在外卖市场有垄断行为。图中可辨识物件：市场分布图、单一颜色的街区、唯一的招牌、监管人员的手。

pos.zh: 垄断的；垄断性的；倾向排除竞争的

senses.title: Resembling a monopoly
senses.definition: showing the qualities of a market or practice controlled by a single seller
senses.definitionCN: 表现出由单一卖方控制的市场或做法所具有的特征
senses.example: The inquiry found monopolistic conditions in the ticket market.
senses.exampleCN: 调查发现票务市场存在垄断性状况。
senses.why: the suffix -istic means resembling or relating to, so the adjective describes a likeness to monopoly rather than its legal existence.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -istic 意为「像……的、与……相关的」，因此这个形容词描述与垄断相似，而非法律上的既成事实。

senses.title: Single-seller in structure
senses.definition: describing a market whose supply comes from one dominant provider
senses.definitionCN: 描述供给来自一个支配性提供者的市场
senses.example: The port is a monopolistic market with one operator.
senses.exampleCN: 这个港口是由一家运营商把持的垄断性市场。
senses.why: economists use the adjective for structures that approach a single seller even without a formal grant.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家用这个形容词描述即使没有正式授予、也接近单一卖方的结构。

senses.title: Conduct that tends to exclude rivals
senses.definition: business conduct that makes it hard for rivals to enter or survive
senses.definitionCN: 使对手难以进入或生存的商业做法
senses.example: Exclusive contracts were judged monopolistic.
senses.exampleCN: 排他合同被判定为垄断性做法。
senses.why: competition law shifts the adjective from structure to conduct, asking whether an act forecloses the market.
senses.whyCN: 竞争法把这个形容词从结构移到行为，追问某一行为是否封闭了市场。

senses.title: Pricing as if there were no rival
senses.definition: setting prices at the level a single seller could sustain without competition
senses.definitionCN: 按单一卖方在无竞争时所能维持的水平定价
senses.example: Monopolistic pricing pushed the price well above cost.
senses.exampleCN: 垄断定价把价格推到远高于成本的水平。
senses.why: the adjective names the price behaviour that the structure makes possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词指结构所使之成为可能的价格行为。

senses.title: Abuse of dominance in competition law
senses.titleCN: 反垄断法语境的滥用支配地位
senses.definition: conduct by a dominant firm that regulators treat as an abuse of its position
senses.definitionCN: 支配性企业作出、被监管者视为滥用其地位的行为
senses.example: The ruling classified the refusal to supply as monopolistic abuse.
senses.exampleCN: 裁决把拒绝供货归类为垄断性滥用。
senses.why: legal usage borrows the adjective because the statute must cover conduct that falls short of a full monopoly.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法借用这个形容词，因为法条须覆盖尚未构成完整垄断的行为。

senses.title: A firm large enough to set terms
senses.titleCN: 规模大到能设定条件的企业
senses.definition: describing a company whose size lets it dictate terms to suppliers or customers
senses.definitionCN: 描述规模使其能对供应商或顾客发号施令的公司
senses.example: A monopolistic buyer can dictate the price it pays farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 垄断性买方能单方面决定付给农民的价钱。
senses.why: the adjective can attach to a buyer as well, since size rather than selling is the key.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也可用于买方，因为关键在于规模而非卖方身份。

senses.title: State-run and exclusive
senses.definition: describing a trade reserved to a government body
senses.definitionCN: 描述由某一政府机构专属经营的行业
senses.example: The salt trade remained monopolistic until the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 盐业直到改革前都保持国家专营的格局。
senses.why: state monopolies supplied the earliest model, and the adjective still fits them.
senses.whyCN: 国家专卖提供了最早的范型，这个形容词至今仍适用于它们。

senses.title: Exclusive in a non-commercial sense
senses.definition: describing any arrangement in which one party shuts others out
senses.definitionCN: 描述任何由一方把他人排除在外的安排
senses.example: The club's monopolistic control of the archive worried historians.
senses.exampleCN: 该俱乐部对档案的排他性控制令历史学者担忧。
senses.why: once detached from markets, the adjective simply marks exclusion by one party.
senses.whyCN: 脱离市场后，这个形容词只标记由一方实施的排除。

intro.en: Monopolistic is an English derivative of monopoly, formed with the suffix complex -ist plus -ic, which reached English through French -istique from Latin -isticus and Greek -istikos. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monopolistic 是 monopoly 的英语派生词，由 -ist 加 -ic 的后缀组合构成；这一组合经法语 -istique 上溯拉丁 -isticus，再上溯希腊 -istikos。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek -istikos formed adjectives from agent nouns, often meaning 'skilled in' or 'concerned with'.
items.cn: 希腊 -istikos 从施事名词构成形容词，常表示「擅长于」或「与……有关」。

items.en: Latin -isticus carried the Greek suffix into learned vocabulary, where it described things belonging to a person or practice.
items.cn: 拉丁 -isticus 把这个希腊后缀带入学术词汇，描述属于某人或某种做法的事物。

items.en: French -istique passed the pattern to English adjectives such as artistic and characteristic.
items.cn: 法语 -istique 把这一模式传给英语形容词，如 artistic 与 characteristic。

items.en: English built monopolist with -ist and then monopolistic with -ic, so the adjective names what the holder does or resembles.
items.cn: 英语先用 -ist 构成 monopolist，再用 -ic 构成 monopolistic，因此这个形容词指持有者的作为或相似特征。

items.en: The adjective appears in nineteenth-century economic and legal writing, when states began regulating exclusive trading privileges.
items.cn: 这个形容词出现在 19 世纪的经济与法律写作中，当时各国开始规制独家贸易特权。

items.en: The exact first printed use is not recorded. Every step of the suffix chain is documented, so no part of the form is reconstructed.
items.cn: 最早印刷用例没有确切记录。后缀链条的每一步都有据可查，因此词形没有重构成分。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same family that name a different part of speech or a different market; group two holds near descriptors of market conduct.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中词性或所修饰市场不同的词；第二组是描述市场行为的近义形容词。

entries.definition: The participle of the verb, meaning that a market has already been taken over; it reports an act, not a standing trait.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去分词，表示市场已被占据；它报告一个动作，而非一种常态特征。

entries.definition: The person or firm holding the position; monopolistic describes the position or conduct, not the holder.
entries.definitionCN: 持有该地位的人或企业；monopolistic 描述地位或行为，而非持有者。

entries.definition: The buyer-side mirror, describing a market with one purchaser; the selling element has been replaced by a buying one.
entries.definitionCN: 买方一侧的镜像词，描述只有一个买主的市场；其中「卖」的成分已换成「买」。

entries.definition: Describing a market of few sellers; the form is parallel, but the first element changes from one to few.
entries.definitionCN: 描述少数卖方的市场；词形平行，但第一成分从「一」变为「少数」。

entries.definition: Describing conduct that harms competition; a regulator may call an act anti-competitive without calling the market monopolistic.
entries.definitionCN: 描述损害竞争的行为；监管者可以称某行为反竞争，而不称该市场垄断。

entries.definition: Holding the largest share or greatest influence; dominance is a precondition that competition law tests separately.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有最大份额或最强影响力；支配地位是竞争法另行检验的前提。

entries.definition: Limiting what others may do; a restrictive clause may or may not create a monopoly.
entries.definitionCN: 限制他人可为之事；限制性条款未必造成垄断。

entries.definition: Open to one party only; exclusivity can be lawful, while monopolistic conduct is the regulated case.
entries.definitionCN: 只对一方开放；排他可以是合法的，而垄断行为才是受规制的情形。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: monopoly + -ist + -ic: the adjective of the holder and the practice.
normal.cn: monopoly + -ist + -ic：由持有者与做法构成的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs monopoly, monopolist, monopolize, monopolization, monopolistic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 monopoly、monopolist、monopolize、monopolization、monopolistic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the legal sense: monopolistic behaviour, monopolistic pricing, monopolistic practices.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律义：垄断行为、垄断定价、垄断做法。

normal.en: The suffix means 'resembling', so the word can describe conduct that is not yet a full monopoly.
normal.cn: 后缀意为「像……的」，因此这个词可以描述尚未构成完整垄断的行为。

normal.en: Its buyer-side twin is monopsonistic.
normal.cn: 它在买方一侧的对应词是 monopsonistic。

abstract.en: Picture a map where every block is painted the colour of one company.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，每个街区都被涂成同一家公司的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a door with one keyhole and one key in the whole town.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，全城只有一把钥匙能开。

abstract.en: Picture a referee who also owns one of the teams.
abstract.cn: 想象一名裁判同时拥有一支参赛队伍。

examples.en: The court described the rebate scheme as monopolistic.
examples.cn: 法院把该返利方案描述为垄断性的。

examples.en: Monopolistic pricing can survive only behind high entry barriers.
examples.cn: 垄断定价只能在进入壁垒很高时维持。

examples.en: Not every dominant firm is monopolistic in the legal sense.
examples.cn: 并非每个支配性企业在法律意义上都是垄断的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「monopoly（垄断）+ istic（……的）」——带垄断味道的 → 垄断性的

root: monopoly（希腊 monos「单独」+ pōlein「卖」，经拉丁 monopolium）+ 后缀 -ist + -ic（经法语 -istique、拉丁 -isticus、希腊 -istikos），构成「具有垄断特征的」形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one likeness: something takes on the shape of a single-seller market, and that shape is then read as general resemblance, structure, conduct, pricing, legal abuse, buyer size, state trade, and finally any exclusion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种「相似」展开：某事物呈现出单一卖方市场的形状，这个形状再被读作总体相似、结构、行为、定价、法律滥用、买方规模、国家经营，最后是任何排除。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a market map painted in one colour, with a single sign left standing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被涂成单一颜色的市场地图，只剩一面招牌立着。

branches.en: LIKENESS AND STRUCTURE: the general resemblance, then the near-single-seller market itself.
branches.cn: 相似与结构：总体相似，以及接近单一卖方的市场本身。

branches.en: CONDUCT AND PRICE: conduct that shuts rivals out, and the price such conduct permits.
branches.cn: 行为与价格：把对手关在门外的行为，以及这种行为所允许的价格。

branches.en: THE LEGAL LABEL: dominance abused rather than a market fully held.
branches.cn: 法律标签：被滥用的支配地位，而非被完整握有的市场。

branches.en: SIZE AND THE STATE: a buyer big enough to set terms, and a trade reserved to government.
branches.cn: 规模与国家：大到能设定条件的买方，以及保留给政府的行业。

branches.en: NON-COMMERCIAL EXCLUSION: one party shutting others out of an archive or a field.
branches.cn: 非商业排除：一方把他人挡在档案或领域之外。

intro.en: The adjective stacks a Greek noun, a Greek-derived agent suffix and an adjective suffix, so each layer can be read on its own.
intro.cn: 这个形容词叠了一个希腊名词、一个希腊来源的施事后缀和一个形容词后缀，因此每一层都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin monopolium is the base noun, and Latin -isticus (from Greek -istikos) supplies the ending seen in artistic and characteristic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 monopolium 是基础名词，拉丁 -isticus（来自希腊 -istikos）提供 artistic 与 characteristic 中可见的结尾。

items.example: One element of the compound means single.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词的一个成分意为「单一」。

items.example: The other element means to sell.
The monopoly ended with the new statute.
items.exampleCN: 新法终结了这项专营权。

items.example: The monopolist raised the access fee.
Two firms monopolized the market.
Monopolization took a decade.
The practice was called monopolistic.
items.exampleCN: 这种做法被称为垄断性的。

items.example: The firm priced its service monopolistically.
items.exampleCN: 这家企业以垄断方式定价。

items.example: The airline market remains oligopolistic.
items.exampleCN: 航空市场仍呈寡头格局。

items.example: Buyers held monopsonistic power over growers.
items.exampleCN: 买方对种植者拥有买方垄断力量。

definition_zh: 降雨；降雨量；一场雨
definition_en: rain falling from the sky, or the amount of rain measured over a period
core_image: 云底压得很低，雨线密密地垂到地面，量筒里的水一寸寸升高
scene: 雨下了一整夜，气象站的量筒里积起半尺深的水。 Heavy rainfall overnight raised the water in the gauge by half a foot.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「落下的雨水」（第 1 个义项：降雨这一事件）；句意为夜间的大雨使量筒里的水升高了半英尺。

pos.zh: 降雨；降雨量；（一场）雨

forms.label: 复数（多场降雨或多次读数）

senses.title: Rain coming down
senses.definition: the fall of rain from clouds
senses.definitionCN: 雨从云中落下这一事件
senses.example: Heavy rainfall overnight raised the water in the gauge by half a foot.
senses.exampleCN: 夜间的大雨使量筒里的水升高了半英尺。
senses.why: Rain plus fall names the event directly: the first element is the substance, the second is its motion.
senses.whyCN: rain 加 fall 直接命名事件：前者是物质，后者是它的运动。

senses.title: The measured depth
senses.definition: the depth of rain that has fallen, measured in millimetres or inches
senses.definitionCN: 已经落下的雨的深度，以毫米或英寸计
senses.example: The city recorded forty millimetres of rainfall in one hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市一小时内记录到四十毫米降雨量。
senses.why: A gauge converts a shower into a depth, and the compound takes on that measured reading.
senses.whyCN: 量筒把一场雨变成一段深度，这个复合词也就承担了这一读数。

senses.title: The yearly total
senses.definition: the total rain a place receives in a year
senses.definitionCN: 某地一年所获得的总雨量
senses.example: The island's annual rainfall supports dense forest.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的年降雨量足以养活茂密的森林。
senses.why: Climate description needs a period, so rainfall becomes an annual figure rather than a single storm.
senses.whyCN: 气候描述需要一个周期，于是 rainfall 成为年度数字，而不是一场暴雨。

senses.title: A season's rain
senses.definition: the rain belonging to a particular season or month
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个季节或月份的雨
senses.example: Most of the region's rainfall arrives between June and September.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区大部分降雨集中在六月到九月之间。
senses.why: Once totals are grouped by month, the word also names the rain attached to a stretch of the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 一旦总量按月分组，这个词也指附着在某段日历上的雨水。

senses.title: Water supply for farming
senses.definition: rain considered as the water source for crops and pastures
senses.definitionCN: 被视为作物与牧场水源的雨水
senses.example: Dry farming depends entirely on natural rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 旱作农业完全依赖自然降雨。
senses.why: For a farmer, rain is not weather but input; the word shifts from the sky to the water budget.
senses.whyCN: 对农民来说，雨不是天气而是投入；这个词于是从天空转到水量收支。

senses.title: Liquid precipitation as a category
senses.definition: in climate science, the liquid form of precipitation as opposed to snow
senses.definitionCN: 气候科学中与降雪相对的液态降水
senses.example: The model separates rainfall from snowfall in mountain zones.
senses.exampleCN: 模型在山地分区中把降雨与降雪分开处理。
senses.why: Classification needs a label for the liquid member, and rainfall supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 分类需要给液态成员一个标签，rainfall 提供了这个标签。

senses.title: Rain in a particular place
senses.definition: the characteristic rain of a named region, as in tropical or coastal rainfall
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定地区的典型雨水，如热带或沿海降雨
senses.example: Coastal rainfall keeps the valleys green long into summer.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海降雨让山谷一直绿到盛夏。
senses.why: Place adjectives attach naturally, because rain is one of the first things people notice about a region.
senses.whyCN: 地点形容词自然附着其上，因为雨是人最先注意到的地方特征之一。

senses.title: Rain produced by cloud seeding
senses.definition: rain that has been encouraged to fall by human intervention
senses.definitionCN: 经人工干预而促使其落下的雨
senses.example: The province counts on seeded rainfall during drought years.
senses.exampleCN: 该省在干旱年份依靠人工增雨。
senses.why: When people can trigger the fall, the same noun names the product of an intervention.
senses.whyCN: 当人能触发这场落下时，同一个名词也指干预的产物。

intro.en: Rainfall is a modern English compound of two native Old English words. The compound itself is recent, while both halves are ancient. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: rainfall 是由两个英语本土的古英语词构成的现代复合词。复合词本身很新，两个构件却很古老。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Rain goes back to Old English regn, from Proto-Germanic *regna-, a word shared by most Germanic languages.
items.cn: rain 源自古英语 regn，出自原始日耳曼语 *regna-，为多数日耳曼语言共有。

items.en: Fall goes back to Old English feallan 'to fall', from Proto-Germanic *fallan, and has always meant a downward movement.
items.cn: fall 源自古英语 feallan「落下」，出自原始日耳曼语 *fallan，一直表示向下的运动。

items.en: The compound rainfall appears in nineteenth-century writing, when weather observation became systematic and totals needed a short name.
items.cn: 复合词 rainfall 出现于十九世纪文献，当时天气观测走向系统化，总量需要一个简短名称。

items.en: Rain gauges and agricultural yearbooks spread the measured sense, so that a place could be described by how much rainfall it received rather than by how often it rained.
items.cn: 雨量筒与农业年鉴推广了测量义，于是描述一个地方可以靠它接收多少降雨量，而不是靠下雨的次数。

items.en: The measured sense expanded with national weather services and the phrase annual rainfall became standard in geography textbooks.
items.cn: 随着国家气象机构的建立，其测量义扩展，annual rainfall 成为地理教科书的固定说法。

note.en: Group one holds compounds built on the same word rain; group two holds words for water falling in other ways.
note.cn: 第一组是以同一个 rain 构成的复合词；第二组是表示水以其他方式落下的词。

entries.definition: A single drop of rain; it names one piece, while rainfall names the whole event or total.
entries.definitionCN: 一滴雨；它指单个水滴，而 rainfall 指整个事件或总量。

entries.definition: The coloured arc seen when sunlight passes through drops; it is a sight caused by rain, not the rain itself.
entries.definitionCN: 阳光穿过水滴时看到的彩色弧；它是雨造成的景象，而不是雨本身。

entries.definition: A storm with heavy rain; it adds the idea of wind and violence that rainfall does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 夹带大雨的风暴；它多了风与猛烈之意，而 rainfall 没有这层意思。

entries.definition: Falling water of every kind, including snow and hail; it is the technical category to which rainfall belongs.
entries.definitionCN: 各种形式落下的水，包括雪与冰雹；它是 rainfall 所属的技术类别。

entries.definition: Very light rain made of tiny drops; it describes an intensity, not an amount over a season.
entries.definitionCN: 由细小水滴构成的毛毛雨；它描述强度，而非一段时间内的总量。

entries.definition: A sudden heavy fall of rain; it stresses the burst, while rainfall can be calm and cumulative.
entries.definitionCN: 突然而降的大雨；它强调爆发，而 rainfall 可以是平缓累积的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the compound is transparent, and its partners are real weather terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：这个复合词的意义一目了然，搭配也都是真实的天气术语。

normal.en: rain + fall: the substance plus its motion, exactly like snowfall and moonlight.
normal.cn: rain + fall：物质加运动，与 snowfall、moonlight 完全同构。

normal.en: rainfall total is the phrase used when the event is converted into a number.
normal.cn: rainfall total 是把事件换算成数字时使用的搭配。

normal.en: annual rainfall is the standard geography phrase for a place's yearly water supply.
normal.cn: annual rainfall 是地理学中描述某地年度水量的标准说法。

normal.en: rainfall and snowfall split the same idea by temperature, and precipitation is the umbrella term.
normal.cn: rainfall 与 snowfall 按温度把同一想法分开，precipitation 则是统称。

normal.en: rain gauge is the instrument that turns rainfall into a reading, pairing the compound with its tool.
normal.cn: rain gauge 是把 rainfall 变成读数的仪器，把这个复合词与工具配在一起。

abstract.en: Abstractly, rainfall is water leaving the sky on a schedule no one controls; the compound names both the leaving and the amount left behind.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，rainfall 是按无人能控制的日程离开天空的水；这个复合词同时命名离开与留下的量。

abstract.en: The same word can be a moment (a heavy fall) or a decade (an annual average), because a gauge can measure either.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既可是一刻（一场大雨），也可是十年（年均值），因为量筒两者都能测。

abstract.en: So rainfall is rain viewed as supply: something that arrives, accumulates and must be counted.
abstract.cn: 所以 rainfall 是把雨看作供给：它到来、累积，并且必须被计量。

examples.en: The northern slope receives twice the rainfall of the southern slope.
examples.cn: 北坡的降雨量是南坡的两倍。

examples.en: A week of steady rainfall replenished the reservoirs.
examples.cn: 一周持续的降雨补足了水库。

examples.en: Gardeners time their planting by the expected rainfall.
examples.cn: 园丁按预期的降雨安排种植时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: rain（雨）+ fall（落下）：雨从天上落下来 → rainfall 降雨、降雨量

root: rain 源自古英语 regn（原始日耳曼语 *regna-），fall 源自古英语 feallan（原始日耳曼语 *fallan）；复合词 rainfall 于十九世纪出现。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow water from sky to ledger: the event of falling, the depth measured, the yearly total, the seasonal share, the farm supply, the liquid category, the regional character and the artificially seeded shower.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让水从天空走到账本：落下的事件、测得的深度、全年总量、季节份额、农业供给、液态类别、地方特征以及人工催下的雨。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water leaves the sky and is caught, first as an event and then as a depth in a gauge.
core.cn: 核心意象：水离开天空并被接住，先是一个事件，然后成为量筒里的一段深度。

branches.en: EVENT AND READING: the shower and the number it leaves in the gauge are one noun.
branches.cn: 事件与读数：一场雨与它在量筒里留下的数字共用一个名词。

branches.en: CALENDAR: grouped by season or by year, rain becomes a schedule.
branches.cn: 日历：按季节或按年份分组，雨就变成一张时间表。

branches.en: SUPPLY: for farming, the same water is an input in the budget.
branches.cn: 供给：对农业而言，同一份水是收支表里的投入。

branches.en: CATEGORY: climate science sets the liquid member beside snow.
branches.cn: 类别：气候科学把液态成员与雪并列。

branches.en: PLACE AND INTERVENTION: rain belongs to a region, and can also be made to fall.
branches.cn: 地方与干预：雨属于某个地区，也可以被人为催下。

intro.en: Rainfall is a native compound, so its family grows by compounding rather than by Latin suffixes: rain + drop, bow, coat, storm, water and gauge.
intro.cn: rainfall 是英语本土复合词，其词族靠复合而非拉丁后缀扩展：rain 加 drop、bow、coat、storm、water、gauge。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic, with no Latin ancestor; the Latin entry list is empty on purpose.
latinIntro.cn: 两个构件都属日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁词条列表按设计留空。

items.example: A raindrop splashed on the hot stone.
items.exampleCN: 一滴雨落在滚烫的石头上溅开了。

items.meaning: the coloured arc formed by sunlight in raindrops
items.meaningCN: 阳光在雨滴中形成的彩色弧（bow 指弓形）
items.example: A rainbow rose over the wet field.
items.exampleCN: 湿漉漉的田野上升起一道彩虹。

items.meaning: a waterproof coat worn in rain
items.example: He folded his raincoat into the bag.
items.exampleCN: 他把雨衣折好放进包里。

items.meaning: a storm accompanied by heavy rain
items.example: The rainstorm closed the mountain road.

items.meaning: water that has fallen as rain, often collected for use
items.meaningCN: 落下的雨水，常被收集利用
items.example: The barrel stores rainwater for the garden.
items.exampleCN: 桶里存着浇园用的雨水。

items.example: The rain gauge was read at dawn.

items.meaning: the summed rainfall over a period
items.meaningCN: 一段时间内累计的降雨总量
items.example: The monthly rainfall total broke a record.

items.meaning: rain made acidic by dissolved pollutants
items.meaningCN: 因溶解污染物而呈酸性的雨，即酸雨
items.example: Acid rain stripped the leaves from the trees.

definition_zh: 地震的；地震引起的；震动的；影响巨大的
definition_en: relating to earthquakes or to the vibrations they send through the ground
core_image: 一条波线从地底某一点向四面扩散，经过之处墙体和地表都在轻微起伏
scene: 地震台网的值班室里，屏幕上一条波形刚刚越过警戒线。 Sensors across the valley recorded seismic activity for three minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 seismic 是「地震的」（第 1 个义项：与地震或地震引起的震动有关）；句意为谷地各处的传感器记录了三分钟的地震活动。

pos.zh: 地震的；地震引起的；震动的；影响巨大的

derivatives.zh: 地震活动性；某地区的地震频度
在地震方面；按抗震方式
地震学（seismo- 组合形式参与构成的学科名）

senses.title: Relating to earthquakes
senses.definition: connected with earthquakes or with the shaking of the earth's crust
senses.definitionCN: 与地震或地壳震动相关的
senses.example: Sensors across the valley recorded seismic activity for three minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 谷地各处的传感器记录了三分钟的地震活动。
senses.why: seismic comes from Greek seismos, a shaking or earthquake, so the adjective simply points to that event.
senses.whyCN: seismic 来自希腊 seismos「震动、地震」，因此这个形容词直接指向那个事件。

senses.title: Concerning seismic waves
senses.definition: describing the elastic waves that travel through rock after a sudden rupture
senses.definitionCN: 描述岩体突然破裂后在岩石中传播的弹性波
senses.example: Seismic waves arrive from the focus in several distinct phases.
senses.exampleCN: 地震波以几个不同震相从震源抵达。
senses.why: once instruments could record the shaking, the adjective was attached to the waves that carry it, not only to the event.
senses.whyCN: 当仪器能记录震动之后，这个形容词就不仅指事件，也用于承载震动的波。

senses.title: Monitoring ground motion
senses.definition: used for instruments, networks or data that detect and measure ground shaking
senses.definitionCN: 用于探测与测量地面震动的仪器、台网或数据
senses.example: The seismic network sent an alert before the strongest shaking arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 地震台网在最强震动到达前发出了警报。
senses.why: a monitoring system is named by what it watches, so seismic became the standard label for earthquake detection.
senses.whyCN: 监测系统按它监视的对象命名，因此 seismic 成了地震探测的标准标签。

senses.title: Imaging the ground by sound
senses.definition: relating to the method that sends artificial vibrations into the ground and reads their echoes
senses.definitionCN: 与向地下发送人工震动并读取回波的方法有关
senses.example: A seismic survey mapped the salt dome under the seabed.
senses.exampleCN: 一次地震勘探测出了海床下的盐丘。
senses.why: the same physics that records earthquakes can be reversed: make a controlled shock and listen to the reflections.
senses.whyCN: 记录地震的同一套物理可以反用：制造可控震动，再听反射。

senses.title: Based on seismic data
senses.definition: derived from recorded ground motion, as in images of rock layers or fault maps
senses.definitionCN: 由记录到的地面运动推得，如岩层图像或断层图
senses.example: The seismic image shows a buried fault beneath the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 地震图像显示三角洲下有一条被掩埋的断层。
senses.why: data is named by the physical signal that produced it, so seismic became a shorthand for the whole imaging method.
senses.whyCN: 数据按产生它的物理信号命名，因此 seismic 成了整套成像方法的简称。

senses.title: Relating to earthquake risk
senses.definition: concerning the probability and expected strength of shaking at a place
senses.definitionCN: 关于某地发生震动的概率与预期强度
senses.example: The building code sets seismic requirements for every new school.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑规范为每所新建学校规定了抗震要求。
senses.why: risk language uses the adjective because the hazard itself is the shaking, not the fault line on a map.
senses.whyCN: 风险语言使用这个形容词，因为危险本身是震动，而不是地图上的断层线。

senses.title: Designed to resist earthquakes
senses.definition: built or fitted so that structures can survive strong shaking
senses.definitionCN: 为使结构能在强烈震动中存留而建造或装配
senses.example: Seismic isolation lets the base move while the floors stay steady.
senses.exampleCN: 地震隔震让底座移动而楼层保持稳定。
senses.why: engineering turns the adjective into a design goal: whatever resists the shaking is called seismic.
senses.whyCN: 工程学把这个形容词变成设计目标：凡是能抵御震动的都冠以 seismic。

senses.title: Figuratively enormous in effect
senses.titleCN: 比喻：影响如同地震般巨大的
senses.definition: having an effect as sudden and far-reaching as an earthquake
senses.definitionCN: 产生的影响如地震般突然而深远
senses.example: The ruling caused a seismic shift in how the industry was financed.
senses.exampleCN: 这项裁决使该行业的融资方式发生了地震般的转变。
senses.why: the figurative sense borrows the scale of an earthquake: not just a change, but one that rearranges the ground under everything.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义借用了地震的规模：不只是变化，而是把一切脚下的地面重新排布。

intro.en: Seismic was formed in English in the nineteenth century from Greek seismos, a shaking, an earthquake, built on the verb seiein, to shake, plus the adjective suffix -ic. It has no Latin ancestor.
intro.cn: seismic 是 19 世纪英语新造词，来自希腊 seismos「震动、地震」，其词根为动词 seiein「摇动」，加形容词后缀 -ic。它没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: Seiein meant to shake or drive by shaking. Its deeper pre-Greek origin is not established, so any Indo-European form for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: seiein 意为「摇动、以摇动驱使」。其希腊语之前的更深来源未获证明，因此为它给出的任何印欧形式都属重构。

items.en: Seismos named a shaking or an earthquake; the same stem appears in seismology and in older medical use for trembling.
items.cn: seismos 指一次震动或地震；同一词干也出现在 seismology，以及较早医学用语中的「颤抖」。

items.en: English scientists coined seismic in the mid nineteenth century to name the study and measurement of earthquakes, at a time when seismology was becoming a science.
items.cn: 19 世纪中叶，英语科学界造出 seismic，用来命名地震的研究与测量，当时地震学正成为一门科学。

items.en: In the twentieth century seismic survey came to mean deliberate sound-wave imaging of rock layers for oil, gas and engineering.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，seismic survey 指为石油、天然气与工程目的，用声波对岩层做主动成像。

items.en: Late modern English extended the adjective to any change of earthquake scale, as in a seismic shift in policy or markets.
items.cn: 现代英语晚期把这个形容词扩展到任何地震级的变化，如政策或市场上的地震式转变。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Greek root of seiein is unsettled, and the earliest printed use of seismic is dated only approximately to the 1850s.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：seiein 的希腊语之前词根尚无定论，seismic 最早的印刷用例也只能约略定在 1850 年代。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Greek shaking stem; group two holds adjectives that describe large earth movements or huge effects.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊「震动」词干的词；第二组是描述大规模地壳运动或巨大影响的形容词。

entries.definition: An older synonym meaning relating to an earthquake; it is now rare beside seismic.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的同义词，意为「与地震有关的」；如今除 seismic 外已罕用。

entries.definition: Built with the Greek negative prefix a-: either free from earthquakes or designed to resist them.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊否定前缀 a- 构成：或指无地震的，或指抗震的。

entries.definition: The frequency and distribution of earthquakes in a region; the noun behind seismic activity.
entries.definitionCN: 某地区地震的频度与分布；即 seismic activity 背后的名词。

entries.definition: Seismo- plus -graph, a writing instrument: the device that draws a record of ground motion.
entries.definitionCN: seismo- 加 -graph「书写」：把地面运动画成记录曲线的仪器。

entries.definition: Relating to the structure of the earth's crust and the plates that move it; tectonic events cause earthquakes but the word does not mean seismic.
entries.definitionCN: 与地壳结构及推动地壳的板块有关；构造事件会引发地震，但该词本身并不等于 seismic。

entries.definition: Literally shaking the earth, but in practice almost always figurative for enormously important; seismic covers both the literal and figurative.
entries.definitionCN: 字面为「摇动大地」，实际几乎总作比喻指「极其重大」；seismic 则兼具字面与比喻两义。

entries.definition: Relating to the physics of the earth as a whole, including gravity, magnetism and heat; seismic is only one branch of it.
entries.definitionCN: 与整个地球的物理有关，包括重力、磁场与热；seismic 只是其中一个分支。

entries.definition: Describing a disastrous outcome; it can describe an earthquake's effects but says nothing about shaking as such.
entries.definitionCN: 描述灾难性后果；可描述地震的影响，但本身并不指震动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek seismos, shaking, plus -ic: the adjective of an earthquake.
normal.cn: 希腊 seismos「震动」加 -ic：地震的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs seismic, seismicity, aseismic, seismograph, seismometer, seismogram, seismology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 seismic、seismicity、aseismic、seismograph、seismometer、seismogram、seismology。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: seismic wave, seismic survey, seismic hazard, seismic design.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：地震波、地震勘探、地震危险、抗震设计。

normal.en: seismo- is the combining form in instrument names, always tied to ground motion.
normal.cn: seismo- 是仪器名称中的组合形式，始终与地面运动相关。

normal.en: The figurative phrase seismic shift is a set expression for a very large change.
normal.cn: 比喻搭配 seismic shift 是「巨大转变」的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped in a pond, but the rings run through rock.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落入池塘，只是涟漪穿过的是岩石。

abstract.en: Picture a city where every table starts sliding at the same instant.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市里每张桌子在同一瞬间开始滑动。

abstract.en: Picture a rulebook rewritten overnight while everyone is still asleep.
abstract.cn: 想象一本规则手册在众人熟睡时被一夜改写。

examples.en: The region has been quiet, with no seismic activity for a decade.
examples.cn: 该地区一直平静，十年来没有地震活动。

examples.en: Seismic reflection revealed a deep basin beneath the plain.
examples.cn: 地震反射探测揭示出平原之下有一个深盆地。

examples.en: The new evidence caused a seismic change in the accepted theory.
examples.cn: 新证据使公认理论发生了地震般的改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「seis（震）+ mic」——大地在抖动 → 地震的、震动的

root: 希腊 seismos「震动、地震」，源自 seiein「摇动」，加形容词后缀 -ic；希腊来源，无拉丁同族，拉丁词条留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the same shaking: first the earthquake itself, then its waves, its monitoring, its use for imaging, its data, its risk, its engineering answer, and finally any change on the same scale.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种震动展开：先是地震本身，继而它的波、监测、成像用途、数据、风险、工程对策，最后是任何同等规模的变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wave front spreading from one point underground, tilting everything it passes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道波前从地下某点扩散，经过之处一切都在倾斜。

branches.en: THE EVENT: seismic points first at the earthquake itself.
branches.cn: 事件：seismic 首先指向地震本身。

branches.en: CARRYING AND WATCHING: waves carry the shaking, instruments watch it.
branches.cn: 承载与监视：波承载震动，仪器监视震动。

branches.en: ACTIVE USE: the same physics is turned into a lamp for the subsurface.
branches.cn: 主动利用：同一套物理被改造为照亮地下的灯。

branches.en: RISK AND RESPONSE: shaking becomes a design load to be resisted.
branches.cn: 风险与应对：震动变成必须抵御的设计荷载。

branches.en: METAPHOR: the scale of an earthquake is lent to social change.
branches.cn: 比喻：把地震的规模借给社会变化。

intro.en: Seismic is a Greek-derived adjective whose combining form seismo- appears at the front of a whole family of earth-science words.
intro.cn: seismic 是希腊来源的形容词，其组合形式 seismo- 出现在整族地球科学词汇的词首。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor: the family goes back to Greek seiein and seismos, and Latin gained only loanwords such as the medical use of tremor.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁语祖先：这个词族上溯希腊 seiein 与 seismos；拉丁语只贡献了如医学用法的 tremor 等借词。

items.exampleCN: seismo- 位于仪器与学科名称的词首。

items.example: The noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The verb supplies the root sei-.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供词根 sei-。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Seismic data guide the drill.

items.exampleCN: 地震活动性低使该场址颇具吸引力。

items.example: Aseismic bearings isolate the hall.
The seismograph traced a long, low pulse.
items.exampleCN: 地震仪描出一条长而低的脉冲。

items.meaning: an instrument that measures ground motion
items.example: The seismometer sat on bedrock.

items.meaning: the record produced by a seismograph
items.example: The seismogram showed two arrivals.
items.exampleCN: 地震记录图显示两个到达震相。

items.example: Seismology grew from early earthquake catalogues.
items.exampleCN: 地震学从早期地震目录发展而来。

senses.title: To name a cause
senses.definition: to say that an event or condition was caused by a particular factor
senses.definitionCN: 指出某一事件或状况由某个特定因素造成
senses.example: Scientists can attribute to volcanic ash the sudden cooling.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家可以把突然降温归因于火山灰。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to assign a share, and a cause is the share of responsibility assigned to one factor.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为分派一份，而原因就是分派给某个因素的那一份责任。

senses.title: To credit a person for something good
senses.definition: to say that a good result was produced by a particular person or group
senses.definitionCN: 认为某个好结果是由某个特定的人或群体带来的
senses.example: The coach will attribute to the captain the team's revival.
senses.exampleCN: 教练会把球队的复苏归功于队长。
senses.why: Credit is a share of honour, and the same verb that assigns a cause also assigns praise.
senses.whyCN: 功劳是一份荣誉，分派原因的那个动词也分派赞扬。

senses.title: To name the author of a work
senses.definition: to say that a painting, book or other work was made by a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 认定一幅画、一部书或其他作品由某个特定的人创作
senses.example: Scholars may attribute to Titian the unsigned portrait.
senses.exampleCN: 学者可能认为那幅未署名的肖像出自提香。
senses.why: A work has an origin, and the verb that assigns a cause to a factor also assigns a work to a hand.
senses.whyCN: 作品有其来处，把原因分派给因素的那个动词也把作品分派给某一双手。

senses.title: To assign a quality to someone
senses.titleCN: 把某种特征归属于某人
senses.definition: to say that a person or thing has a particular quality or characteristic
senses.definitionCN: 认为某人或某物具有某种特定的品质或特征
senses.example: People can attribute to the breed a calm temperament.
senses.exampleCN: 人们可以把温和的性情归属于这一品种。
senses.why: A quality is treated as a share laid on a subject, the same arithmetic of assignment as a cause.
senses.whyCN: 品质被当作放在某个主体身上的一份，与原因的分派是同一套算法。

senses.title: To trace a symptom to its cause
senses.definition: to say that a symptom or illness was produced by a particular pathogen or condition
senses.definitionCN: 认为某种症状或疾病由某个特定病原体或状况引起
senses.example: Doctors may attribute to the tick the sudden fever.
senses.exampleCN: 医生可能把突然发热归到蜱虫身上。
senses.why: Medical tracing repeats the general pattern: an effect is handed back to the thing that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 医学溯源重复着同一模式：结果被交还给产生它的东西。

senses.title: To link a climate effect to warming
senses.titleCN: 把气候现象归因于变暖
senses.definition: in climate science, to state that a particular weather or ice change was made more likely by global warming
senses.definitionCN: 在气候科学中，指认定某一特定天气或冰情变化因全球变暖而更可能发生
senses.example: The panel will attribute to warming the shrinking glacier.
senses.exampleCN: 专家组会把冰川退缩归因于变暖。
senses.why: Climate research made attribution a technical term: the share of risk assigned to a named driver.
senses.whyCN: 气候研究把「归因」变成了术语：把风险的一份分派给某个被指名的驱动因素。

senses.title: To trace something to an origin
senses.definition: to show that a word, custom or lineage belongs to a particular source or family
senses.definitionCN: 表明一个词、一种习俗或一支血脉属于某个特定源头或族系
senses.example: Linguists can attribute to the same root two distant dialects.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学家可以把两种相距很远的方言都追溯到同一个词根。
senses.why: Origin is a place on a family tree, and the verb places a thing on that tree by assigning it a branch.
senses.whyCN: 源头是谱系树上的一个位置，这个动词通过分派一个枝系把事物放到那棵树上。

senses.title: To blame a fault on someone
senses.definition: to say that a fault, failure or bad outcome was caused by a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 认为某个过失、失败或坏结果由某个特定的人造成
senses.example: The inquiry may attribute to the pilot the final error.
senses.exampleCN: 调查可能把最后的失误归咎于飞行员。
senses.why: When the assigned share is blame, the same neutral verb takes on a hostile edge without changing its structure.
senses.whyCN: 当被分派的那一份是责难时，同一个中性的动词就带上敌意，而结构并未改变。

intro.en: Attribute comes from Latin attribuere, to assign or allot, formed from ad-, to, and tribuere, to divide or give, which goes back to tributum, a tax. The same root produced tribute, contribute and distribute. English took the verb in the sixteenth century, and attribute to became the usual frame for naming a cause, an author or a fault.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「attribuere」「分派、给予」，由「ad-」「朝向」和「tribuere」「分配、给予」构成，而「tribuere」出自「tributum」「税」。同一词根还产生「tribute」、「contribute」与「distribute」。英语在十六世纪引入这个动词，短语「attribute to」成为指出原因、作者或过错的常用框架。

items.en: The noun meant a tax or a payment divided among people, the concrete image of parting out a sum.
items.cn: 这个名词意为税或按人分摊的款项，是「把钱分出去」的具体意象。

items.en: The verb meant to divide, allot or grant, and it named the act of giving each party its share.
items.cn: 这个动词意为分配、分给、授予，指给每一方一份的动作。

items.en: The prefix meant to or towards, and it directed the share towards a particular recipient.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为朝向，把那一份指向某个特定的接受者。

items.en: The compound meant to assign or impute something to a person or thing, the direct source of the English verb.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为把某物分派或归到某人某物身上，是这个英语动词的直接来源。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth century and used it for assigning causes, qualities, authors and blame.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，用于分派原因、品质、作者与过错。

items.en: The phrase attribute to fixed the target of the assignment, and it now appears in science, law, art history and ordinary argument.
items.cn: 短语「attribute to」固定了分派的目标，如今出现在科学、法律、艺术史与日常论辩中。

note.en: The first group gathers words built with the same root or a neighbouring prefix; the second group gathers verbs of assigning a cause, an author or a fault.
note.cn: 第一组收录由同一词根或相近前缀构成的形式；第二组收录表示分派原因、作者或过错的动词。

entries.definition: The act of saying who or what something comes from, and the name given to that origin.
entries.definitionCN: 指认定某物来自谁或什么的动作，也指由此给出的出处。

entries.definition: Able to be explained by or credited to a particular cause.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够由某一特定原因解释或归于其名下的。

entries.definition: To give money, effort or ideas towards a common purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 指为共同目的拿出钱财、努力或想法。

entries.definition: To divide something and give it out among several people or places.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物分开并分发给若干人或地方。

entries.definition: A payment made by one ruler or group to another as a sign of submission.
entries.definitionCN: 指一方统治者或群体向另一方缴纳以示臣服的贡品。

entries.definition: To say that something belongs to or is caused by a particular person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为某物属于或由某个特定的人或物引起。

entries.definition: To say that someone is responsible for a good result.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为某人应对某个好结果负责。

entries.definition: To say that someone or something is at fault for a bad result.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为某人或某物应对坏结果负责。

entries.definition: To give a particular role, cause or value to someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某个角色、原因或数值分派给某人或某物。

entries.definition: To say that a fault or quality belongs to someone, often unfairly.
entries.definitionCN: 指把过失或品质归到某人身上，常含不公之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin act of handing out a share, the real prefix family, and the real phrases of cause, credit and fault.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拉丁语中「分出一份」的动作、真实的前缀词族，以及原因、功劳与过错的真实搭配。

normal.en: Tribuere is to divide and give out, so attribute to is to hand a share back to its source.
normal.cn: 「tribuere」是分开并发放，因此「attribute to」就是把一份交还给它该去的地方。

normal.en: Contribute, distribute and tribute all carry the same offering of a share.
normal.cn: 「contribute」「distribute」与「tribute」都带着同一个「献出一份」的意思。

normal.en: People attribute a painting to a painter, a fever to a tick, and a failure to a pilot; the frame never changes.
normal.cn: 人们把画归给画家，把发热归给蜱虫，把失败归给飞行员；框架始终不变。

normal.en: The word often takes the cause as its target: attribute to the storm the delay.
normal.cn: 这个词常把原因放在短语之后：把延误归因于暴风雨。

normal.en: In climate reports, attribution means the share of risk that a named factor can claim.
normal.cn: 在气候报告里，归因指某个被指名的因素可以认领的那一份风险。

abstract.en: Attribution is a family tree drawn on the fly: every effect gets a branch, every work gets a hand.
abstract.cn: 归因是随手画出的谱系树：每个结果都得到一根枝，每件作品都得到一双手。

abstract.en: The verb is neutral until the share is shame; then assigning a cause becomes assigning blame.
abstract.cn: 这个动词本中性，直到那一份是羞耻；此时分派原因就变成分派责难。

abstract.en: To attribute well is to resist the nearest hand: distance makes the difference between evidence and blame.
abstract.cn: 善加归因就是抵抗最近的那双手：距离划出证据与责难之间的界线。

examples.en: The report will attribute to bad wiring the loss of power.
examples.cn: 报告会把断电归因于线路不良。

examples.en: Many readers attribute to Homer the whole epic.
examples.cn: 许多读者认为整部史诗出自荷马。

examples.en: Officials may attribute to heavy rain the closed road.
examples.cn: 官员可能把道路封闭归因于大雨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「阿特崔比优特·图」——按份派回去，功劳或错处落到该去的人头上：归因、归功

root: 拉丁语「attribuere」「分派、给予」=「ad-」「朝向」+「tribuere」「分配、给予」←「tributum」「税」；同根有「contribute」「distribute」「tribute」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one frame of assignment: naming a cause, crediting a person, naming an author, assigning a quality, tracing a symptom, attributing a climate effect, tracing an origin, and placing blame.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个「分派」框架：指出原因、把功劳归于某人、认定作者、归属品质、追溯症状、归因气候现象、溯源系属、分派过错。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brush draws a new name back to an older branch on a family scroll and marks where that branch comes from.
core.cn: 核心意象：朱笔把新添的名字画回家谱上较老的枝，并标明这一枝的来处。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: a factor receives its share of responsibility, whether a local event or a warming climate.
branches.cn: 原因：某个因素得到它的一份责任，无论是局部事件还是气候变暖。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the same share becomes honour for a captain or shame for a pilot.
branches.cn: 人：同一份既可成为队长的荣誉，也可成为飞行员的羞耻。

branches.en: THE WORK AND THE QUALITY: a creation is given a hand, and a trait is given a subject.
branches.cn: 作品与品质：创作被配上一双手，特征被配上一个主体。

branches.en: THE SYMPTOM: a fever is sent back to the creature that caused it.
branches.cn: 症状：发热被送回到引起它的生物。

branches.en: THE LINEAGE: a word or custom is set on a branch of a larger family tree.
branches.cn: 谱系：一个词或习俗被放到更大谱系树的某一枝上。

intro.en: Attribute is built from a Latin verb of dividing and giving, and its family spreads across money, praise and blame.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个表示分配与给予的拉丁动词构成，其词族散布在钱财、赞誉与责难之间。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies tribuere and attribuere, with tributum behind them; the same root reaches English through tribute, contribute and distribute.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「tribuere」与「attribuere」，它们背后是「tributum」；同一词根经「tribute」、「contribute」与「distribute」进入英语。
