definition_en: coming from the source it claims to come from, and therefore real, reliable, or faithful to an original
core_image: 一只手在旧画角落找到画家的签名——不是像，而是本人留下的那一笔
scene: 厨房里蒸汽升腾，一位厨师对来客轻声开口。 A chef tells a visitor: This is an authentic recipe, copied by hand from my grandmother's notebook.
sceneCN: 这里 authentic 指「地道的、正宗的」（第 2 个义项：照着原产地做法）；句意：这是一份地道的食谱，是从我祖母的笔记本上亲手抄下来的。画面里有手写食谱、面粉和一口旧锅。

pos.zh: 真正的；真迹的；地道的；可信的；真诚的

forms.label: 形容词原级（比较级用 more）

senses.title: Real, not false
senses.definition: real and not false, invented, or imitated
senses.definitionCN: 真实而非虚假、编造或仿制的
senses.example: The museum bought the letter only after proving it authentic.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆在证明这封信为真迹之后才买下它。
senses.why: Greek authentikos meant 'original, principal', from authentes 'one who acts on his own authority'. A genuine thing is one that can stand as its own source, not a copy of another.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 authentikos 意为「原初的、主要的」，出自 authentes「凭自己权威行事者」。真正的东西能作为自身的来源站住，而不是另一个东西的复制。

senses.title: Of the original place
senses.definition: made or done in the original regional way
senses.definitionCN: 按原地区的做法制作或进行的
senses.example: She learned to cook authentic Sichuan food in Chengdu.
senses.exampleCN: 她在成都学会了做地道的川菜。
senses.why: Once the source is a place rather than a person, 'original' means 'as done there'. The adjective moves from legal proof to cultural fidelity.
senses.whyCN: 一旦来源从一个人变成一个地方，「原初」就变成「照着那里做」。这个形容词从法律证明滑向了文化忠实。

senses.title: Worthy of belief
senses.titleCN: 可信的：对得上发生的事
senses.definition: of an account or report, deserving to be believed
senses.definitionCN: （叙述或报道）值得相信的
senses.example: The book gives an authentic account of life in the trenches.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对战壕生活作了可信的记述。
senses.why: Mid-14th-century English also recorded 'real, entitled to acceptance as factual'. The word judges a statement's correspondence to what happened, so 'reliable' became its natural neighbour.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪中叶的英语还记录了「真实的、可被接受为事实的」义。这个词判断陈述与已发生之事的对应关系，所以 reliable 成了它的天然邻居。

senses.title: From the maker's own hand
senses.definition: being the original work, not a reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 是原作而非复制品的
senses.example: Only an authentic signature adds value to the print.
senses.exampleCN: 只有真迹签名才会给这幅版画增值。
senses.why: The legal document model — this is the very instrument, sealed by its maker — was transferred to art. The adjective then answers 'whose hand made this?'
senses.whyCN: 法律文书的模型——就是这一份，由制作者盖印——被移到艺术上。这个形容词于是回答「这是谁的手做的？」

senses.title: Sincere, not performed
senses.definition: of a person or feeling, sincere and not performed for an audience
senses.definitionCN: （人或情感）真诚而不为观众表演的
senses.example: His surprise seemed authentic, not staged for the cameras.
senses.exampleCN: 他的惊讶看起来是真的，不是为镜头摆拍的。
senses.why: The existential sense of 'own' rather than 'copied' became a moral one: an authentic feeling belongs to the person who shows it. The word now praises the absence of pretence.
senses.whyCN: 「属于自己的」而非「抄来的」这一存在主义义变成道德义：真实的情感属于显露它的人。这个词如今称赞的是「没有伪装」。

senses.title: Authoritative, in older use
senses.titleCN: 权威的：古义里的「正式授权」
senses.definition: authoritative or duly authorized, an older sense now rare
senses.definitionCN: 有权威或经正式授权的，此为现已罕见的旧义
senses.example: The decree was authentic because the king's seal was on it.
senses.exampleCN: 这道敕令是正式有效的，因为上面有国王的印章。
senses.why: This was the word's first English sense, from Medieval Latin authenticus, translating Greek authentikos. Authority and authenticity were one idea before truth separated them.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最早的英语义，来自中世纪拉丁语 authenticus，是对希腊语 authentikos 的翻译。在「真」把两者分开之前，权威与真实原本是一个概念。

senses.title: Legally valid
senses.definition: executed in the proper legal form, so as to be valid
senses.definitionCN: 按正当法律形式作成因而有效的
senses.example: An authentic will must be signed before two witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 一份有法律效力的遗嘱必须在两名见证人面前签署。
senses.why: Latin authenticus named documents that could be enforced. The adjective still appears in legal phrases where formal execution, not sincerity, is what counts.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 authenticus 指可被强制执行的文件。这个形容词仍出现在法律短语里，在那里算数的是正式作成，而不是真诚。

senses.title: Faithful to a period
senses.titleCN: 原真的：复原到原来的演法
senses.definition: reproducing the original style, instruments, or materials of a period
senses.definitionCN: 复现某一时期的原风格、原乐器或原材料的
senses.example: The ensemble performs authentic Baroque music on gut strings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个乐团用羊肠弦演奏原真的巴洛克音乐。
senses.why: The question 'is this the original?' becomes a programme: reconstruct period practice. 'Authentic performance' is a claim about method, not about a single surviving object.
senses.whyCN: 「这是不是原件」这个问题变成了一套方法：复原当时的做法。authentic performance 是对方法的宣称，而不是对某件幸存实物的宣称。

senses.title: Firmly evidenced
senses.definition: of evidence, firmly established and not merely probable
senses.definitionCN: （证据）确凿成立、不只是可能的
senses.example: Police need authentic evidence, not a rumour from the street.
senses.exampleCN: 警方需要确凿的证据，而不是街头的传言。
senses.why: From 'entitled to acceptance as factual', the adjective hardens into an evidential standard. What is authentic has a source that can be produced and checked.
senses.whyCN: 从「可被接受为事实」出发，这个形容词硬化为一条证据标准。真实的东西有一个可以拿出来、可以核查的来源。

intro.en: Authentic arrived in English as a word about authority and only later settled into a word about truth. Its Greek ancestor names a person who acts on his own authority; a document, an object, or a feeling is authentic when it can claim that kind of source.
intro.cn: authentic 初到英语时讲的是权威，后来才落定为讲「真」的词。它的希腊祖先指「凭自己权威行事的人」；一份文件、一件物品或一种情感，只要能声称有那样的来源，就是 authentic。

items.en: authentikos 'original, genuine, principal' came from authentes 'one acting on one's own authority', autos 'self' + hentes 'doer, being'. The root behind hentes, PIE *sene- (2) 'to accomplish', is reconstructed, with no written record, so it is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: authentikos「原初的、真正的、主要的」出自 authentes「凭自己权威行事者」，即 autos「自己」+ hentes「行事者、存在者」。hentes 背后的词根 PIE *sene- (2)「完成」是重构形式，没有书面记录，标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: authenticus carried the Greek adjective into Latin, where it attached to documents, seals and authorities. The word certified a source before it described a fact.
items.cn: authenticus 把希腊形容词带进拉丁语，在那里附着于文件、印章与权威。这个词先证明来源，后来才描述事实。

items.en: autentique 'authentic; canonical' (Modern French authentique) entered English through Norman and central French, losing the Greek -h- on the way.
items.cn: autentique「真正的；正典的」（现代法语 authentique）经诺曼法语与中部法语进入英语，一路丢掉了希腊语的 h。

items.en: autentik is recorded as 'authoritative, duly authorized' and, in the same century, as 'real, entitled to acceptance as factual'. The -th- spelling was restored later by learned reference to Latin and Greek.
items.cn: autentik 被记录为「有权威的、经正式授权的」，同一世纪也指「真实的、可被接受为事实的」。后来学者参照拉丁语和希腊语，把 -th- 的拼写补了回来。

items.en: The factual sense won: authentic came to mean 'real, not fictitious', while genuine stressed that the reputed author is the real one. OED notes that the 18th-century distinction is not etymological.
items.cn: 「符合事实」义胜出：authentic 指「真实、非虚构」，而 genuine 强调所署作者确为其人。OED 指出，18 世纪的那套区分并不符合词源。

items.en: Authentic extended to regional food, heritage sites, the 'authentic self', and historically informed performance, so that fidelity to an origin became a value in its own right.
items.cn: authentic 扩展到地方饮食、文化遗产地、「真实的自我」和历史复原演奏，对来源的忠实本身成了一种价值。

note.en: The first group shares the authent- stem or the -entic sound; the second group names things that are real or believable, which authentic can mean in different contexts.
note.cn: 第一组共享 authent- 词干或 -entic 读音；第二组是「真」或「可信」的近义词，authentic 在不同语境下可以对应它们。

entries.definition: the quality of being genuine or trustworthy. It is authentic plus -ity, the abstract noun.
entries.definitionCN: 真实性；真品性。它是 authentic 加 -ity 构成的抽象名词。

entries.definition: in a genuine, original, or sincere way.
entries.definitionCN: 真实地；地道地；真诚地。

entries.definition: the process of proving that something or someone is genuine.
entries.definitionCN: 认证；鉴定；身份验证。

entries.definition: not genuine; imitated or performed.
entries.definitionCN: 不真实的；伪造的；造作的。

entries.definition: the creator of a work, from Latin auctor. The sound is close, the family is not.
entries.definitionCN: 作者；创作者，出自拉丁语 auctor。读音相近，词族不同。

entries.definition: real and exactly what it is said to be, especially of a person's feelings or an object's origin.
entries.definitionCN: 真正的；名副其实的，尤指情感或物品来源。

entries.definition: actually existing or happening, not imagined or pretended. It is the plain word behind authentic.
entries.definitionCN: 真实的；实际存在的。它是 authentic 背后那个朴素的词。

entries.definition: existing from the beginning, or being the first version rather than a copy.
entries.definitionCN: 最初的；原作的；非复制的。

entries.definition: convincing enough to be believed. It matches authentic in the 'reliable account' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 可信的；有说服力的。对应 authentic 的「可信记述」义。

entries.definition: allowed by law or by the rules, or reasonable and genuine. It covers authentic's legal and sincere edges.
entries.definitionCN: 合法的；正当的；合理的。它覆盖 authentic 的法律义与真诚义边缘。

normalIntro.en: authent- is the Greek stem for 'acting on one's own authority'; -ic makes it an adjective. The whole family turns on who has the right to speak for a thing.
normalIntro.cn: authent- 是希腊语「凭自己权威行事」的词干；-ic 使它成为形容词。整个词族都围绕「谁有权为某物作证」。

normal.en: authentic = author-like: both suggest someone standing behind the thing, though the two words are not related.
normal.cn: authentic 与 author 形似：都暗示有一个「人」站在东西背后，不过两词并不同源。

normal.en: An authentic signature is a signature you can put under a microscope.
normal.cn: authentic signature 是一枚可以放到显微镜下查验的签名。

normal.en: authentic food tastes of the place, not of the airport.
normal.cn: authentic 的食物有那个地方的味道，而不是机场的味道。

normal.en: Authentic and genuine are siblings in use: genuine asks whose hand, authentic asks what warrant.
normal.cn: authentic 与 genuine 是用法上的兄弟：genuine 问「谁的手」，authentic 问「什么凭证」。

normal.en: The -th- is a learned repair: French left it out, English put it back from the Latin.
normal.cn: 中间的 -th- 是一次学术修补：法语漏掉了它，英语照拉丁语补回。

abstract.en: The word begins as a seal and ends as a feeling: authority moved from the document to the person.
abstract.cn: 这个词从一枚印章开始，到一种情感结束：权威从文件移到了人身上。

abstract.en: Authentic always compares two things: the copy and the source it claims to come from.
abstract.cn: authentic 永远在比较两样东西：复制品，以及它声称来自的来源。

abstract.en: To call a thing authentic is to accept a chain of custody, even when the chain is only a recipe.
abstract.cn: 称某物 authentic，就是接受一条来源链，哪怕这条链只是一份食谱。

examples.en: The dealer could not prove that the vase was authentic.
examples.cn: 经销商无法证明这只花瓶是真品。

examples.en: We wanted an authentic meal, so we ate where the drivers eat.
examples.cn: 我们想吃一顿地道的饭，于是去了司机们吃饭的地方。

examples.en: Her anger was authentic and passed in a minute.
examples.cn: 她的愤怒是真的，一分钟就过去了。

dict_mnemonic.text: authentic 拆成 author（作者）+ tic——作者亲手交出的一笔，当然是「真迹的、真正的」

root: 源自希腊语 authentikos「原初的、真正的、主要的」← authentes「凭自己权威行事者」（autos「自己」+ hentes「行事者」），经拉丁语 authenticus 与古法语 autentique 进入英语；核心是「有一只手或一个来源为它作证」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses answer one question in different rooms: a letter, a kitchen, a courtroom, a gallery, a diary, a concert. In each, authentic asks whether the thing comes from the hand or place it claims.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项在不同房间里回答同一个问题：一封书信、一间厨房、一座法庭、一间画廊、一本日记、一场音乐会。每个场景里，authentic 都在问：这东西是否出自它声称的那只手或那个地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the maker's own hand, leaving a mark that a copy cannot leave.
core.cn: 核心意象：制作者本人的手，留下复制品留不下的痕迹。

branches.en: REAL AND VALID: a thing that is what it claims to be, and an instrument legally executed.
branches.cn: 真实与有效：名副其实的东西，以及依法作成的文书。

branches.en: TRUSTWORTHY: an account that fits the facts, and evidence firm enough to stand on.
branches.cn: 可信：与事实相符的叙述，以及足以站住的证据。

branches.en: ORIGINAL IN PLACE AND HAND: food cooked the local way, and a work from the maker's own hand.
branches.cn: 地方与手上的原初：按当地做法烹制的食物，以及出自本人之手的作品。

branches.en: THE SINCERE AND THE AUTHORIZED: a feeling that belongs to its bearer, and an old sense of official authority.
branches.cn: 真诚与授权：属于本人的情感，以及官方权威的旧义。

branches.en: FIDELITY TO A PERIOD: performance or restoration that follows the original practice.
branches.cn: 对时代的忠实：遵循原初做法的演出或修复。

intro.en: authentic is authent- (Greek authentes, 'one acting on his own authority') + -ic (adjective). Its family shows -ity, -ly, -ate, -ation, -or, and the negative prefix in-; author is a look-alike from Latin auctor, not a relative.
intro.cn: authentic 是 authent-（希腊语 authentes「凭自己权威行事者」）+ -ic（形容词）。词族展示 -ity、-ly、-ate、-ation、-or 以及否定前缀 in-；author 是出自拉丁语 auctor 的形近词，并非同族。

latinIntro.en: Greek authentikos gave Latin authenticus; authenticare 'to make valid' gave authenticate; -icus and -itat- are the suffixes behind English -ic and -ity.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 authentikos 给出拉丁语 authenticus；authenticare「使有效」给出 authenticate；-icus 与 -itat- 是英语 -ic 与 -ity 背后的后缀。

items.example: The document is authentic, not a nineteenth-century copy.
items.exampleCN: 这份文件是真件，不是 19 世纪的复制品。

items.example: The authenticity of the relic is disputed.
items.exampleCN: 这件圣物的真伪有争议。

items.meaning: in a genuine or original way
items.example: The dish is cooked authentically, with no shortcuts.
items.exampleCN: 这道菜做得地道，没有偷工减料。

items.meaning: to establish the genuineness of something
items.example: The signature was authenticated by a handwriting expert.
items.exampleCN: 签名经笔迹专家鉴定为真。

items.example: Authentication of the painting took six weeks.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画的鉴定用了六周。

items.meaning: one who or that which verifies
items.example: The token works as a second authenticator.
items.exampleCN: 这个令牌充当第二重认证器。

items.example: The label warned buyers of inauthentic goods.
items.exampleCN: 标签提醒买家提防仿冒商品。

items.meaning: the quality of being false or staged
items.example: Critics noted the inauthenticity of the accent.
items.exampleCN: 评论者指出那口音不自然。

items.example: The word authenticness was current in the 1620s.
items.exampleCN: authenticness 一词在 17 世纪 20 年代通用。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 真正的；原初的；有权威的

latinEntries.structure: auctor (noun; not the source of authentic)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 创始者；作者（并非 authentic 的来源）

definition_zh: 按比例地；相称地；按份额地；等比例地；按比例代表制地；均衡地
definition_en: in a way that keeps the same relation or share, so that each change or portion matches another
core_image: 两根柱子沿着同一条斜线一起升降，刻度始终对齐
scene: 这里指「按比例地」。 The rooms were proportionally arranged, with the largest sitting room placed beside the largest bedroom.
sceneCN: 这里 proportionally 是「匀称地、按相称比例地」（第 8 个义项：布置的尺寸关系相互匹配）；句意：这些房间布置得比例相称，最大的客厅挨着最大的卧室。图中可辨识物件：由大到小排开的门、对齐的墙角线。

pos.zh: 按比例地；相称地；按份额地；等比例地

senses.title: Changing by the same fraction
senses.definition: so that a change in one amount produces a matching change in another at a fixed rate
senses.definitionCN: 指一个量的变化使另一量按固定比率产生相配的变化
senses.example: Wages rose proportionally with the increase in output.
senses.exampleCN: 工资随产量的增加而按比例上升。
senses.why: The adverb turns proportional into a statement about change: whatever happens to one quantity, the other is adjusted by the same fraction.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把 proportional 变成对变化的陈述：无论一个量怎样变，另一个量都按同一分数调整。

senses.title: In a fitting degree
senses.definition: to a degree that fits the seriousness or size of something else
senses.definitionCN: 达到与另一事物的严重程度或规模相配的程度
senses.example: The judge insisted that the penalty be proportionally severe to the harm caused.
senses.exampleCN: 法官坚持处罚要与造成的损害程度相称。
senses.why: Here the share is moral rather than numerical: the response is weighed so that it does not overmatch or undermatch the wrong.
senses.whyCN: 这里的份额是道德性的而非数字性的：回应经过权衡，既不超过也不低于过错。

senses.title: Shared out by shares
senses.definition: divided among people or groups according to agreed shares
senses.definitionCN: 按约定份额在人或者群体之间分配
senses.example: The estate was divided proportionally among the four heirs.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产在四位继承人之间按比例分配。
senses.why: Distribution uses the oldest share sense: each person receives the fraction that belongs to them, and the adverb describes how the division was made.
senses.whyCN: 分配用的是最古老的份额义：每人得到属于自己的那一份，副词描述划分的方式。

senses.title: Scaled without distortion
senses.definition: enlarged or reduced so that every dimension keeps its relation to the others
senses.definitionCN: 放大或缩小后每个尺寸都保持与其他尺寸的关系
senses.example: Enlarge the drawing proportionally so that the circles stay round.
senses.exampleCN: 把图等比例放大，让圆仍然是圆的。
senses.why: Scaling proportionally means applying one multiplier to every measurement. Nothing stretches, because all the fractions between dimensions remain the same.
senses.whyCN: 等比例缩放意味着对每个测量值施加同一个倍数。因为没有哪个尺寸被单独拉伸，所以尺寸之间的分数关系保持不变。

senses.title: Plotted as a true rate
senses.definition: represented on a graph so that distances show the actual ratio rather than a distorted one
senses.definitionCN: 在图上表示时使距离反映真实比值而非被扭曲的比值
senses.example: If you plot the two variables proportionally, the slope shows the true growth rate.
senses.exampleCN: 如果把两个变量按比例作图，斜率就显示真实的增长率。
senses.why: Graphic display also depends on shares: a chart drawn proportionally gives every unit the same length, so slopes can be trusted.
senses.whyCN: 图形展示同样依赖份额：按比例绘制的图表给每个单位相同长度，因此斜率可信。

senses.title: Seats matched to votes
senses.definition: by a system that gives each party seats in rough proportion to its votes
senses.definitionCN: 按使各党席位大致与其选票成比例的制度
senses.example: In that assembly, seats are allocated proportionally rather than winner-take-all.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个议会中，席位按比例分配，而不是赢者通吃。
senses.why: Electoral use applies the adverb to allocation: the seats are handed out proportionally, so a party's share of seats tracks its share of votes.
senses.whyCN: 选举用法把这个副词用于分配：席位按比例发放，因此一个政党的席位份额追随其选票份额。

senses.title: Sampled at the true rate
senses.definition: drawn or weighted so that each subgroup appears in its actual share of the whole
senses.definitionCN: 抽取或加权使每个子群按其在整体中的实际份额出现
senses.example: The researchers sampled proportionally from each age group to avoid bias.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者从每个年龄组按比例抽样，以避免偏差。
senses.why: Statistics uses the same logic: if one district holds a quarter of the households, it should supply a quarter of the sample, and the adverb says this was done.
senses.whyCN: 统计学使用同一逻辑：如果一个区占四分之一的住户，它就应提供四分之一的样本，副词说明正是这样做的。

senses.title: With harmonious dimensions
senses.definition: in a way that keeps the parts of a design or space in pleasing relation
senses.definitionCN: 指使设计或空间的各部分保持悦目的关系
senses.example: The furniture was proportionally sized so that the small room never felt crowded.
senses.exampleCN: 家具尺寸比例得当，小房间从不显得拥挤。
senses.why: Design judges shares by the eye: parts arranged proportionally look calm, because no element crowds or dwarfs its neighbours.
senses.whyCN: 设计用眼睛判断份额：各部分按比例安排看起来沉稳，因为没有元素挤压或压过邻居。

intro.en: Proportionally is proportional plus the adverb suffix -ly. The base goes back to the Latin phrase pro portione, 'according to the share', and the noun proportio. English took the adjective from French, then added its own -ly to make the adverb.
intro.cn: proportionally 是 proportional 加副词后缀 -ly。其根基可回溯到拉丁短语 pro portione“按份额”与名词 proportio。英语从法语借入形容词，再自己加 -ly 构成副词。

items.en: Portio meant 'a share, an allotted part'. Every sense of the adverb still assumes that something has been divided into shares.
items.cn: portio 意为“份额、分得的部分”。副词的每个义项都仍假定某物已被分成若干份。

items.en: The phrase meant 'according to the share'. It described any arrangement in which each part received its due amount.
items.cn: 这个短语意为“按份额”，描述每一部分各得其应有数量的任何安排。

items.en: Proportio named the relation between shares, and Late Latin proportionalis turned it into an adjective.
items.cn: proportio 命名各份之间的关系，晚期拉丁语 proportionalis 把它变成形容词。

items.en: French proportionnel supplied the English adjective proportional, first used for fitting arrangement and then for exact ratios.
items.cn: 法语 proportionnel 提供了英语形容词 proportional，最初用于恰当排列，后用于精确比值。

items.en: The English suffix -ly, from Old English -lice, turned proportional into an adverb of manner: in a proportional way.
items.cn: 英语后缀 -ly 源自古英语 -lice，把 proportional 变成方式副词：以按比例的方式。

items.en: Measurement, sampling and proportional representation all made the adverb common in technical writing.
items.cn: 计量、抽样与比例代表制都使这个副词在技术写作中变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the adverb from the adjective, the noun and the near-twin proportionately. The meaning group compares ways of corresponding.
note.cn: 形近组区分副词与形容词、名词及近似的 proportionately；词义组比较不同的“相对应”方式。

entries.definition: having a fixed relation or fitting size. It describes the thing, while proportionally describes how something is done.
entries.definitionCN: 具有固定关系或合适大小的。它描述事物，而 proportionally 描述做事的方式。

entries.definition: a share or the relation between parts. It is the noun behind the whole family.
entries.definitionCN: 份额或各部分之间的关系。它是整个词族背后的名词。

entries.definition: in a fitting or fair degree. It leans toward suitability, while proportionally leans toward exact ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 以合适或公平的程度。它偏向“适宜”，而 proportionally 偏向精确比值。

entries.definition: in a way that is out of proportion. The negative prefix reverses the alignment the base word requires.
entries.definitionCN: 以不成比例的方式。否定前缀反转了基础词所要求的对齐。

entries.definition: in a matching way. It says two things move together without promising a fixed ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 以相配的方式。它说两事物一起变化，但不保证固定比值。

entries.definition: to a degree equal to something else. It stresses equality of measure, often in pay or reward.
entries.definitionCN: 达到与另一事物相等的程度。它强调尺度相等，常用于薪酬或报酬。

entries.definition: in equal amounts or without variation. It means equal shares, while proportionally means shares that match a ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 以相等数量或不变化地。它指平均份额，而 proportionally 指符合某一比值的份额。

entries.definition: when compared with something else. It names a comparison but not a fixed proportion.
entries.definitionCN: 与某物比较而言。它命名比较，但不含固定比例。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the image of two columns moving on one slope, then let the adverb describe how shares are kept in changing, dividing, scaling and sampling.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩保留两根柱子沿同一斜线移动的画面，再让副词描述在变化、分配、缩放与抽样中如何守住份额。

normal.en: Hear the endings: proportional is the adjective, proportionally the adverb that answers 'how?'.
normal.cn: 听清词尾：proportional 是形容词，proportionally 是回答“如何”的副词。

normal.en: Two columns rise together on one slope: whatever one does, the other does by the same fraction.
normal.cn: 两根柱子沿同一斜线上升：一根怎样，另一根就按同一分数怎样。

normal.en: Cut a cake proportionally and the child with the bigger share gets the bigger slice, not the same slice.
normal.cn: 按比例分蛋糕，份额大的孩子得到更大的那块，而不是一样大的块。

normal.en: Resize a picture proportionally and faces stay faces; resize one side only and faces stretch.
normal.cn: 等比例改图片尺寸，脸还是脸；只改一边，脸就被拉长。

normal.en: Allocate seats proportionally and the seat chart becomes a smaller copy of the vote chart.
normal.cn: 按比例分配席位，席位图就成了选票图的缩小复制。

abstract.en: The adverb never stands alone: it always implies a second term hidden in the sentence, the thing it is proportional to.
abstract.cn: 这个副词从不孤立存在：它总暗含句子里藏着的第二项，也就是它所成比例的对象。

abstract.en: Keep the scale metaphor: proportionally means one ruler is used for every part, never a different ruler per part.
abstract.cn: 记住尺子的比喻：按比例意味着所有部分共用一把尺，而不是每部分各用一把。

abstract.en: Notice how the same word serves exact science and rough fairness: the ratio may be measured or judged.
abstract.cn: 注意同一个词既服务精确科学，也服务粗略公平：比值可以被测量，也可以被判断。

examples.en: The number of staff grew proportionally with the number of patients.
examples.cn: 员工人数随病人数量按比例增长。

examples.en: The map was scaled proportionally so that distances remained reliable.
examples.cn: 地图按等比例缩放，因此距离仍然可靠。

examples.en: Funds were distributed proportionally to the size of each department.
examples.cn: 资金按各部门规模的比例分配。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“扑罗破身呢哩”：两份破口一起变大，边破边补，始终成比例。

root: 拉丁 pro portione“按份额”（portio 份额）派生 proportionalis，英语形容词 proportional 加 -ly 成副词；核心是“按同一分数对应变化”。

sensesIntro.en: Each sense answers 'how?' with the same rule: keep the shares aligned. The adverb can describe quantities that move together, penalties that fit, estates that are divided, drawings that are scaled, graphs that are plotted, seats that follow votes, samples that mirror the population, and rooms that sit well together.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都用同一条规则回答“如何”：让各份保持对齐。这个副词可以描述一起变动的数量、相称的处罚、被分配的遗产、被缩放的图、被绘制的图表、追随选票的席位、映照总体的样本，以及相互协调的房间。

core.en: An action is performed so that every share stays in its fixed relation to the others.
core.cn: 某动作被执行时，使每一份都保持与其他份的固定关系。

branches.en: MEASURE: amounts and plotted distances change by one common fraction.
branches.cn: 计量：数量与绘图距离按同一个分数变化。

branches.en: FIT: penalties and rooms are judged to be in due relation.
branches.cn: 相称：处罚与房间被判断为处于恰当关系。

branches.en: ALLOCATE: money and seats are handed out by share.
branches.cn: 分配：金钱与席位按份额发放。

branches.en: SCALE: one multiplier is applied to every dimension.
branches.cn: 缩放：对每个尺寸施加同一个倍数。

branches.en: SAMPLE: each subgroup enters in its true share.
branches.cn: 抽样：每个子群按真实份额进入。

intro.en: Proportionally is a Latin share noun with an adjective suffix and an English adverb suffix. The items below show the same base in adjective, noun, near-synonym and negation.
intro.cn: proportionally 是拉丁“份额”名词加形容词后缀、再加英语副词后缀。下列条目展示同一词基的形容词、名词、近义词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the share noun and the derived relation noun. They explain why every form in this family refers back to an allotted portion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出“份额”名词与派生的关系名词，解释为什么这一词族的每个形式都指回一份分配额。

items.example: Costs rise proportionally with distance.
items.exampleCN: 成本随距离按比例上升。

items.example: The fee is proportional to income.
The proportion of salt to water matters.
The answer was proportionate to the question.
items.exampleCN: 回答与问题的分量相称。

items.example: The court reviewed the proportionality of the measure.
items.exampleCN: 法院审查该措施是否相称。

items.example: Small firms were disproportionately affected.
items.exampleCN: 小企业受到不成比例的影响。

items.example: Punishments should be applied proportionately.

items.meaning: adjusting shares to a fixed relation
items.example: The mixer handles the proportioning of sand and cement.
items.exampleCN: 搅拌机负责砂与水泥的配比。

definition_zh: 编程语言；程序设计语言
definition_en: a formal notation in which instructions for a computer are written
core_image: 白板上写满箭头与括号，两行不同风格的符号被圈起来作对比
scene: 教室里，一块白板上写满箭头与括号，两行不同风格的符号被圈起来作对比。 Students compared a programming language built for statistics with one designed for web pages.
sceneCN: 这里 programming language 指用来书写计算机指令的形式化记号系统（第 1 个义项：书写计算机指令的记号系统）；句意：学生们把一门为统计而设计的编程语言与一门为网页而设计的编程语言作了比较。图中可辨识物件：白板、箭头、括号、两个圈。

pos.zh: 编程语言；程序设计语言

senses.title: A notation for computer instructions
senses.titleCN: 书写计算机指令的记号系统
senses.definition: a formal system of symbols and rules in which a person writes what a computer must do
senses.definitionCN: 由符号与规则构成、供人书写计算机须做什么的形式系统
senses.example: Every programming language must define both what is allowed and what it means.
senses.exampleCN: 每门编程语言都必须规定什么写法合法、以及它的含义。
senses.why: the phrase joins the activity of programming to the general word for a system of signs, so its core sense is simply the sign system used for that activity.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把「编程」这项活动与泛指符号系统的「语言」拼在一起，核心义就是这项活动所用的符号系统。

senses.title: A particular named language
senses.definition: one specific language such as a named language with its own compiler or interpreter
senses.definitionCN: 某门具体语言，如有自己编译器或解释器的具名语言
senses.example: The course teaches one programming language in depth rather than five in passing.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课深入教一门编程语言，而不是走马观花教五门。
senses.why: users usually mean a single product when they say a language, because each one has its own grammar and toolchain.
senses.whyCN: 使用者说「一门语言」时通常指单个成品，因为每门都有自己的语法与工具链。

senses.title: A family sharing a paradigm
senses.definition: a group of languages built on one style of organizing computation, such as the functional or object-oriented family
senses.definitionCN: 按同一种组织计算的方式构成的一组语言，如函数式或面向对象语族
senses.example: The functional programming language family treats functions as ordinary values.
senses.exampleCN: 函数式编程语族把函数当作普通值来对待。
senses.why: languages inherit features from one another, so the phrase also names a lineage rather than a single product.
senses.whyCN: 语言之间会相互继承特征，因此这个短语也指一条谱系，而非单个成品。

senses.title: Its grammar and meaning as a study
senses.titleCN: 作为研究对象的语法与语义
senses.definition: the formal grammar and semantics of such notation, studied as a mathematical object
senses.definitionCN: 这类记号系统的形式语法与语义，被当作数学对象来研究
senses.example: Programming language theory asks which programs can be proved correct.
senses.exampleCN: 编程语言理论研究哪些程序可以被证明正确。
senses.why: once the notation is written down precisely, it can be analysed like any formal system, and the phrase names that object of study.
senses.whyCN: 记号一旦被精确写下，就能像任何形式系统一样被分析，短语于是指这个研究对象。

senses.title: A low-level notation
senses.definition: a language whose operations map closely onto machine instructions, such as assembly
senses.definitionCN: 操作与机器指令紧密对应的语言，如汇编
senses.example: Assembly is a programming language, but a programmer rarely writes a whole system in it.
senses.exampleCN: 汇编是一门编程语言，但程序员很少用它写整个系统。
senses.why: the phrase covers depth as well as breadth: closeness to the hardware is a matter of degree, not of being a language or not.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语既涵盖广度也涵盖深度：离硬件近不近是程度问题，而不是算不算语言的问题。

senses.title: A high-level notation
senses.definition: a language whose statements are far from machine detail and closer to human reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 语句远离机器细节、更接近人的推理的语言
senses.example: A high-level programming language hides memory addresses behind named variables.
senses.exampleCN: 高级编程语言用具名变量把内存地址藏起来。
senses.why: the same phrase describes the opposite end of the scale, because what matters is that instructions are written in a notation at all.
senses.whyCN: 同一个短语也描述另一端，因为关键在于指令确实是用某种记号写成的。

senses.title: A notation for one narrow domain
senses.definition: a language designed for one problem area, such as querying data or typesetting
senses.definitionCN: 为某一问题领域设计的语言，如查询数据或排版
senses.example: A domain-specific programming language can be small and still be complete for its task.
senses.exampleCN: 领域特定的编程语言可以很小，却对其任务而言是完整的。
senses.why: narrowing the domain does not remove the language, it only limits what the notation must express.
senses.whyCN: 缩小领域并不取消「语言」的身份，只是限制了这套记号必须表达什么。

senses.title: A notation for controlling a machine
senses.definition: a language used to write movement or operation sequences for a device rather than a general computer
senses.definitionCN: 为设备而非通用计算机编写动作或操作序列的语言
senses.example: The lathe reads a programming language written as a list of tool movements.
senses.exampleCN: 车床读取一种写成刀具动作清单的编程语言。
senses.why: the phrase follows the word program wherever it goes, including machines that never run a general operating system.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语跟着 program 这个词走，包括那些从不运行通用操作系统的机器。

intro.en: The phrase is a twentieth-century compound of two older words: programming from Greek programma, and language from Latin lingua. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语是二十世纪由两个更老的词合成的复合词：programming 出自希腊语 programma，language 出自拉丁语 lingua。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin lingua meant tongue and then language. It passed through Old French langue into English language, keeping both the bodily and the abstract sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lingua 先指舌头，再指语言。它经古法语 langue 进入英语 language，同时保留身体义与抽象义。

items.en: The other half goes back to Greek programma, a written notice, built from pro-, before, and graphein, to write.
items.cn: 另一半可追到希腊语 programma「书面通告」，由 pro-「在前」与 graphein「书写」构成。

items.en: Programming named the act of writing machine instructions from the 1940s, giving the compound its first half.
items.cn: 自 1940 年代起，programming 指编写机器指令的行为，为复合词提供了前半。

items.en: The full phrase appears with the first stored-program machines, when people needed to distinguish the notation from the computer and from natural language.
items.cn: 完整短语随第一批存储程序机器出现，因为人们需要把这套记号与计算机本身、与自然语言区分开。

items.en: As languages multiplied, the phrase stayed general while names such as Fortran, Lisp and C filled in the particular.
items.cn: 语言一多，这个短语保持泛指，而 Fortran、Lisp、C 等专名承担具体指称。

items.en: Both halves are documented: the second from Latin lingua, the first from Greek programma. The first use of the full phrase is dated only approximately, and any older Indo-European source for lingua is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：两半都有文献依据，后半出自拉丁语 lingua，前半出自希腊语 programma；完整短语最早使用的年代只有约数，lingua 更早的印欧语来源属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the two halves of the phrase and their near relatives; the second group names neighbouring notions of code, syntax and notation.
note.cn: 第一组是短语的两半及其近亲；第二组是与代码、语法、记号相邻的概念。

entries.definition: The activity of writing code; alone it names the work, while the full phrase names the notation used in it.
entries.definitionCN: 指编写代码的活动；单独用时指工作，完整短语指工作中使用的记号系统。

entries.definition: Any system of signs, including speech; the phrase narrows it to the signs a computer can execute.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何符号系统，包括口语；短语把它收窄为计算机能执行的符号。

entries.definition: The person who writes in the language; a language is the medium, a programmer is the user.
entries.definitionCN: 指用这门语言书写的人；语言是媒介，程序员是使用者。

entries.definition: A single body of instructions; a programming language is the notation that many such bodies are written in.
entries.definitionCN: 指一套指令；编程语言是许多这样的指令集所用的记号。

entries.definition: The text actually written; it is what a programming language produces, not the language itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指实际写出的文本；它是编程语言的产物，不是语言本身。

entries.definition: The rules that decide which strings are well formed; syntax is one part of a programming language, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 决定哪些字符串合法的规则；语法是编程语言的一部分，而非全部。

entries.definition: Any agreed system of symbols for writing something down; a programming language is a notation built for execution.
entries.definitionCN: 任何约定用来书写某物的符号系统；编程语言是为执行而建的记号系统。

entries.definition: A notation that labels the structure of a document rather than instructing a machine; often confused with programming languages.
entries.definitionCN: 标注文档结构的记号，而不是给机器下指令；常与编程语言混淆。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real halves, the real fixed phrases and the real distinctions, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的构件、真实的固定搭配与真实的分界，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Programming is the activity, language is the sign system: together they name the notation used to write code.
normal.cn: programming 是活动，language 是符号系统：合起来就是写代码所用的记号系统。

normal.en: The family runs program, programming, programmer, language and linguistic.
normal.cn: 同族词有 program、programming、programmer、language 与 linguistic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: high-level, low-level, general-purpose, domain-specific.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出谱系：高级、低级、通用、领域特定。

normal.en: Latin lingua gave language, and English kept both tongue and language in one word.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lingua 给出 language，英语把「舌头」与「语言」留在了同一个词里。

normal.en: A markup language labels a document; a programming language tells a machine what to do.
normal.cn: 标记语言标注文档；编程语言告诉机器做什么。

abstract.en: Picture two chalk circles on a board, each holding a different dialect of the same intention.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上两个粉笔圈，各自装着同一种意图的不同方言。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that a machine can read but a poet cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一句机器读得懂、诗人却读不懂的话。

abstract.en: Picture a grammar book whose examples run when you turn the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一本语法书，翻页时书里的例子就运行起来。

examples.en: A programming language is defined as much by its rules as by its keywords.
examples.cn: 编程语言由规则界定，其重要性不亚于关键字。

examples.en: The team chose a programming language with a strong type system.
examples.cn: 团队选了一门类型系统强的编程语言。

examples.en: Teaching a programming language without projects leaves the syntax abstract.
examples.cn: 教编程语言而不做项目，语法就始终抽象。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）来（gram）明（ming）＋语言」——把步骤说明白所用的那套语言

root: 希腊 pro-「在前」+ graphein「书写」→ programma → 法语 programme → 英语 program → programming；拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」→ 古法语 langue → 英语 language；两词合为 programming language。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses travel from the general notation to one named language, a family, a formal object of study, and then down and across the scale to low-level, high-level, domain-specific and machine-control notations.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从泛指记号出发，走到某门具名语言、一个语族、一个形式研究对象，再沿尺度下探与横移，落到低级、高级、领域特定与机器控制这几类记号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board covered with arrows and brackets, with two different dialects circled side by side for comparison.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块写满箭头与括号的白板，两种不同方言被圈在一起作对比。

branches.en: THE NOTATION ITSELF: symbols plus rules for writing what a computer must do.
branches.cn: 记号本身：符号加规则，用来书写计算机该做什么。

branches.en: PARTICULAR AND FAMILY: one named product, and the lineage of products built on one paradigm.
branches.cn: 单个与谱系：一个具名成品，以及建立在同一范式上的一脉成品。

branches.en: FORMAL OBJECT: grammar and meaning written precisely enough to be proved about.
branches.cn: 形式对象：语法与语义被精确到可以作证明的程度。

branches.en: LEVELS: the same phrase covers assembly at one end and named variables at the other.
branches.cn: 层次：同一短语一端涵盖汇编，另一端涵盖具名变量。

branches.en: NARROW USE: from a single problem domain to a single machine that never runs a general system.
branches.cn: 窄用：从单一问题领域到一台从不运行通用系统的机器。

intro.en: The phrase is two complete words joined by English syntax: a Greek-derived noun with -ing, and a Latin-derived noun with its own history.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个完整单词由英语句法连接：一个希腊来源名词加 -ing，一个拉丁来源名词带着自己的历史。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies lingua for the second half and programma for the first; the English endings -ing and -age do the joining work.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语为后半提供 lingua，为前半提供 programma；英语词尾 -ing 与 -age 承担连接工作。

items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词同时涵盖器官与其用途。

items.example: English kept the bodily and abstract senses together.
items.exampleCN: 英语把身体义与抽象义留在一起。

items.example: The ending turns langue into a name for a whole system.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 langue 变成整套系统的名称。

items.example: The first half of the compound is itself a gerund.

items.meaning: the notation used to write code

items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把这套记号与机器、与口语区分开。

definition_zh: 利他主义；无私；为他人着想的行为
definition_en: the belief or practice of caring for others' welfare more than one's own, often at personal cost
core_image: 一个人把手里最后一块面包递出去，自己的影子却留在空盘子上
scene: 洪水退去后，志愿者把自己的帐篷让给带孩子的家庭，自己在屋檐下坐了一夜。 Her quiet altruism surprised no one who knew her.
sceneCN: 这里 altruism 指把他人的福祉放在自己之前的无私行为（第 1 个义项：无私关怀）；句意为她安静无声的利他之举，认识她的人都不意外。

pos.zh: 利他主义；无私；利他行为

senses.title: Selfless concern for others
senses.definition: the attitude of caring about other people's welfare without expecting a reward
senses.definitionCN: 关心他人福祉而不期待回报的态度
senses.example: Her altruism was rooted in a childhood of shared scarcity.
senses.exampleCN: 她的无私源于童年时共同经历的匮乏。
senses.why: The word was coined as a moral counterweight to egoism: one pole names the self, the other names the other person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被造出来，是为了与利己主义相抗衡：一极命名自我，另一极命名他人。

senses.title: Helping at personal cost
senses.definition: an act that benefits another person while costing the helper time, money or safety
senses.definitionCN: 使他人受益、却让帮助者付出时间、金钱或安全的行为
senses.example: He performed an act of altruism by paying her tuition anonymously.
senses.exampleCN: 他匿名替她付学费，做了一件利他之举。
senses.why: The core is not a feeling but a transfer: something passes from the helper to the helped, and the helper keeps the loss.
senses.whyCN: 核心不是感受，而是转移：某物从帮助者转到受助者，而帮助者留下损失。

senses.title: Biological altruism
senses.definition: in biology, behaviour that lowers an individual's own fitness while raising another's
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，指降低个体自身适应度却提高他者适应度的行为
senses.example: Biologists study altruism in ants that die defending the colony.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家研究蚂蚁为保卫群体而死这种利他行为。
senses.why: A gene's survival can be served by helping relatives, so the cost to one body may still be a gain to the shared line.
senses.whyCN: 基因的延续可以通过帮助亲属实现，因此一个个体的代价仍可能是共同血脉的收益。

senses.title: A moral principle
senses.definition: a principle that tells people to weigh others' interests equally with their own
senses.definitionCN: 要求人们把他人的利益与自身利益同等权衡的原则
senses.example: The lecture contrasted altruism with utilitarianism.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座把利他主义与功利主义对照讲解。
senses.why: Once an attitude becomes a rule, it can be taught and argued about, which is why it appears in ethics textbooks.
senses.whyCN: 当一种态度变成规则，它就可以被教授和争论，因此出现在伦理学教科书里。

senses.title: Charitable giving
senses.definition: donating money, goods or time to strangers without direct benefit
senses.definitionCN: 向陌生人捐赠金钱、物品或时间而无直接收益
senses.example: The foundation was built on the altruism of a few donors.
senses.exampleCN: 这个基金会建立在少数捐赠者的无私之上。
senses.why: Modern charity makes the transfer large and anonymous, so the old word is stretched to cover gifts to people one will never meet.
senses.whyCN: 现代慈善让转移变得巨大而匿名，于是这个旧词被扩展到「给永远不会见面的人送礼」。

senses.title: Everyday kindness
senses.definition: small helpful acts in ordinary life that ask for no return
senses.definitionCN: 日常生活中不求回报的小小帮助
senses.example: Offering a seat on a crowded train is a small act of altruism.
senses.exampleCN: 在拥挤的火车上让座，是一件小小的利他之举。
senses.why: The scale shrinks but the shape stays: a cost is taken on so that another person's moment improves.
senses.whyCN: 规模缩小了，但形状不变：接受一份代价，让另一个人的时刻变好。

senses.title: Organizational altruism
senses.definition: a company or institution giving up some advantage for the good of a wider group
senses.definitionCN: 公司或机构为更大群体的利益放弃部分优势
senses.example: The firm's decision to share its patent was praised as corporate altruism.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司决定共享专利，被称赞为企业利他。
senses.why: An institution repeats the personal pattern at a larger scale: it gives up an advantage so that a wider group benefits.
senses.whyCN: 机构在更大尺度上重复个人的模式：放弃一项优势，让更广泛的群体受益。

senses.title: A philosophical idea
senses.definition: the philosophical claim that disinterested action for others is possible and morally valuable
senses.definitionCN: 认为为他人的无私行为既可能又有道德价值的哲学主张
senses.example: The debate asked whether altruism can ever be entirely disinterested.
senses.exampleCN: 这场辩论追问利他是否可能完全不带私心。
senses.why: The final step is abstract: once the transfer is studied as a claim about human nature, it becomes a question for philosophy.
senses.whyCN: 最后一步是抽象化：当这种转移被当作关于人性的主张来研究，它就成了哲学问题。

intro.en: Altruism is a modern coined word, not an inherited one. It was built in French from a Latin word for 'other'.
intro.cn: altruism 是一个现代新造词，而不是继承来的词。它在法语中用拉丁语「他人」一词构造而成。

items.en: English adopted altruism in the mid 19c. as the direct opposite of egoism in moral and social writing.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪中期吸收 altruism，在道德与社会文本中作为 egoism 的直接对立词。

items.en: The French philosopher Auguste Comte coined altruisme around 1830 from autrui 'other people'.
items.cn: 法国哲学家奥古斯特·孔德约在 1830 年用 autrui「他人」造出 altruisme。

items.en: Autrui comes from the Old French phrase altrui, a case form of autre 'other'.
items.cn: autrui 来自古法语短语 altrui，是 autre「其他」的格变形式。

items.en: The Latin source is alter 'the other of two', which also gives English alternative and alternate.
items.cn: 其拉丁语来源是 alter「两者中的另一个」，它也产生了英语 alternative 与 alternate。

items.en: Comte's coinage was meant to name a secular virtue, so the word entered English already carrying a philosophical programme.
items.cn: 孔德的造词意在命名一种世俗美德，因此这个词进入英语时已带着一套哲学纲领。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root for 'other'; the second group names related moral qualities.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「他人」词根；第二组列出相关的道德品质。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the word to 'other people' and to the picture of handing something over.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把这个词和「他人」以及「把东西递出去」的画面绑在一起。

normal.en: Altruism contains alter, Latin for 'other': the focus is on the other person.
normal.cn: altruism 里有 alter，拉丁语意为「其他」：焦点在他人身上。

normal.en: Picture the last piece of bread leaving your hand; that transfer is the word.
normal.cn: 想象最后一块面包离开你的手；那次转移就是这个单词。

normal.en: The ending -ism marks a principle, so altruism is both an act and a belief.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ism 标记一种原则，所以 altruism 既是行为也是信念。

normal.en: Pair it with egoism: ego is self, alter is other.
normal.cn: 把它和 egoism 配对记：ego 是自我，alter 是他人。

normal.en: Say the first syllable as 'alt', as if you are handing over an alternative life.
normal.cn: 把第一个音节读成 alt，好像你在交出另一种人生。

abstract.en: A transfer with a cost: the helper loses something so the helped gains.
abstract.cn: 带代价的转移：帮助者失去一些，受助者得到一些。

abstract.en: Biology reframes the cost as a gain for shared genes.
abstract.cn: 生物学把这个代价重新解释为共享基因的收益。

abstract.en: When the transfer is anonymous and large, it becomes charity.
abstract.cn: 当转移匿名且规模巨大时，它就成了慈善。

examples.en: Her altruism led her to fund the clinic anonymously.
examples.cn: 她的无私使她匿名资助了这家诊所。

examples.en: Reciprocal altruism can explain cooperation among unrelated animals.
examples.cn: 互惠利他可以解释无亲缘关系动物之间的合作。

examples.en: The essay asks whether pure altruism is possible.
examples.cn: 这篇文章追问纯粹的利他是否可能。

definition_zh: 双语的；使用两种语言的；双语并用的（也可作名词：双语者）
definition_en: using or written in two languages, or able to speak two languages
core_image: 一张对开的告示纸，左半边与右半边写着同样内容却用两种文字，中间用一条细线分开
scene: 社区公告栏上贴着一张对开的告示，左右两半内容相同，文字却不同。 Every bilingual form in the office carried the same sentence twice.
sceneCN: 这里指「同时使用两种语言的」（第 1 个义项：涉及两种语言并用）；句意为办公室里的每份双语表格都把同一句话写了两遍。可辨识物件：告示、对开纸、两种文字、公告栏。

pos.zh: 双语的；使用两种语言的
双语者（可数）

senses.title: Using two languages
senses.definition: describing a thing, service or activity that works in two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述以两种语言运作的事物、服务或活动
senses.example: The bilingual help desk answers in Mandarin and English.
senses.exampleCN: 双语服务台用普通话与英语应答。
senses.why: the word pairs a prefix for 'two' with the Latin word for tongue, so it counts two languages exactly.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把表「二」的前缀与拉丁语表「舌头」的词相连，精确地数两种语言。

senses.title: A person who speaks two languages
senses.definition: describing someone who can use two languages in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 描述能在日常生活中使用两种语言的人
senses.example: She grew up bilingual and still dreams in both.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小双语成长，至今仍用两种语言做梦。
senses.why: a person who carries the pair through a whole life is the human face of the count.
senses.whyCN: 把这一对语言带过一生的人，是这个数目的「人面」。

senses.title: A text or sign in two languages
senses.titleCN: 用两种语言写成的文本或标牌
senses.definition: printed or displayed in two languages at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时以两种语言印刷或展示
senses.example: The bilingual label lists every ingredient twice.
senses.exampleCN: 双语标签把每种成分列出两遍。
senses.why: two languages printed side by side make the pair visible.
senses.whyCN: 两种语言并排印出，就让这一对变得可见。

senses.title: Bilingual education
senses.definition: schooling in which two languages serve as media of instruction
senses.definitionCN: 以两种语言作为教学语言的教育
senses.example: Bilingual education delayed the shift to the majority language.
senses.exampleCN: 双语教育推迟了向多数语言的转换。
senses.why: a school that teaches in two languages turns the count into a curriculum.
senses.whyCN: 用两种语言教学的学校，把这个数目变成课程。

senses.title: A bilingual community or region
senses.definition: describing a place where two languages are in everyday use
senses.definitionCN: 描述两种语言在日常中并用的地方
senses.example: The valley has been bilingual since the railway arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路开通以来，这条山谷一直双语并存。
senses.why: a whole place can hold the pair for generations, so the adjective describes geography as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 整个地方能把这一对保留几代，因此这个形容词既描述人也描述地理。

senses.title: Bilingual processing in the mind
senses.definition: describing research on how one mind stores and switches between two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述对同一心智如何储存并切换两种语言的研究
senses.example: Bilingual speakers separate their languages by context, not by effort.
senses.exampleCN: 双语说话者按场合区分语言，而不是靠费力控制。
senses.why: a mind that holds two systems is the pair studied from inside.
senses.whyCN: 容纳两套系统的心智，是从内部研究的「这一对」。

senses.title: A bilingual dictionary or resource
senses.definition: a reference that gives equivalents in two languages
senses.definitionCN: 给出两种语言对应说法的工具书
senses.example: The bilingual dictionary marks which word fits which register.
senses.exampleCN: 这本双语词典标出哪个词属哪种语域。
senses.why: a dictionary exists to place one language beside the other.
senses.whyCN: 词典的存在，就是把一种语言放在另一种旁边。

senses.title: Bilingual policy or rights
senses.definition: describing official arrangements that guarantee services in two languages
senses.definitionCN: 描述保障以两种语言提供服务的官方安排
senses.example: Bilingual policy made every statute readable in both tongues.
senses.exampleCN: 双语政策使每项法规都能以两种语言阅读。
senses.why: a promise made in law must appear in both tongues, which turns the count into an obligation.
senses.whyCN: 法律作出的承诺必须以两种语言出现，这就把数目变成义务。

intro.en: Bilingual comes from Latin bilinguis 'two-tongued', built on bis 'twice' and lingua 'tongue, language'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁 bilinguis「双舌的」，由表「两次」的成分与 lingua「舌头、语言」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue' and, by extension, 'language'. Its deeper origin is unsettled and no older attested form is agreed.
items.cn: lingua 指「舌头」，引申为「语言」。其更深来源无定论，也没有公认的更早书证形式。

items.en: Bilinguis meant 'two-tongued'. In Roman usage it could also mean 'double-tongued', that is, deceitful, a sense that English did not keep.
items.cn: bilinguis 意为「双舌的」。在罗马用法中它也可指「两面三刀的」，即欺骗性的，这一含义英语没有保留。

items.en: English formed the modern adjective in the nineteenth century, when schooling and censuses made two-language populations visible.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪形成这个现代形容词，当时学校教育与人口普查使双语人群变得可见。

items.en: The twentieth century gave the word a policy life, naming programs that teach in two languages.
items.cn: 二十世纪赋予这个词政策生命，用来指以两种语言教学的项目。

items.en: Psychology and neuroscience later used it for the mental organisation of two language systems.
items.cn: 心理学与神经科学后来用它指两套语言系统在心智中的组织方式。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin root is unknown, and the first English use of the modern sense is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定：拉丁语之前的词根不明，这个现代义在英语中最早使用的年代只能约略推定。

note.en: Group one holds the counting words that are constantly confused; group two holds terms about two-language arrangements.
note.cn: 第一组是常被混淆的计数词；第二组是关于两种语言安排的术语。

entries.definition: Using several languages, often without a fixed count; bilingual is the exact two.
entries.definitionCN: 指使用多种语言，常不限定数目；双语则精确指两种。

entries.definition: Using a single language; it is the opposite pole of the same counting series.
entries.definitionCN: 指只使用一种语言，是同一计数序列的另一端。

entries.definition: The state or practice of having two languages; the adjective describes what the noun names.
entries.definitionCN: 指拥有两种语言的状态或实践；形容词则描述名词所指的情形。

entries.definition: A rare word for a person who speaks two languages; bilingual is far commoner as the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指会说两种语言者的罕用名词；双语一词作名词更常见。

entries.definition: A common label for two-language school programs; it is a compound rather than a Latin borrowing.
entries.definitionCN: 指双语学校项目的常见标签，属复合词而非拉丁借词。

entries.definition: A literal English rendering of the Latin word; in older use it could also mean deceitful.
entries.definitionCN: 是那个拉丁词的直译英语说法；旧用法中也可指欺骗性的。

entries.definition: Using two dialects of one language, a narrower case than two separate languages.
entries.definitionCN: 指使用同一种语言的两种方言，范围比两种独立语言更窄。

entries.definition: The act of moving between languages in conversation; bilingual describes the capacity behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 指会话中在语言间切换的行为；双语描述其背后的能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means two and the root means tongue, so the word literally has two tongues.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「二」，词根意为「舌头」，因此这个词字面上就是「有两条舌头」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases attach it to services: bilingual signs, forms, help desk.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它挂到服务上：双语标识、双语表格、双语服务台。

normal.en: It sits exactly in the middle of the counting ladder: one, two, many.
normal.cn: 它正好在计数阶梯的中间：单语、双语、多语。

normal.en: The family runs bilingualism, bilingually, bilinguals, multilingual, monolingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「双语现象」「以双语方式」「双语者」「多语的」「单语的」。

normal.en: A split notice with the same sentence twice is the picture to hold.
normal.cn: 一张左右分栏、同一句话写两遍的告示，是要留住的画面。

abstract.en: Picture two doors side by side, both opening into the same room.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的两道门，都通向同一个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a mind with two indexes to the same world.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头脑，为同一个世界备有两套索引。

abstract.en: Picture a single sentence walking across a thin line and changing its clothes.
abstract.cn: 想象同一句话跨过一条细线，换了一身衣服。

examples.en: Bilingual ballots were introduced after the court ruling.
examples.cn: 法院裁决之后，双语选票开始启用。

examples.en: Children in bilingual programs read in both languages by nine.
examples.cn: 参加双语项目的孩子到九岁已能用两种语言阅读。

examples.en: The bilingual dictionary distinguishes formal from everyday words.
examples.cn: 这本双语词典区分正式词与日常词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拜林圭尔」——拜两条舌头所赐，两种话都能说，这就是双语的。

root: 拉丁 bilinguis「双舌的」由表「两次」的成分与 lingua「舌头、语言」构成；罗马用法中亦可指「两面三刀的」，该贬义未被英语保留。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses pair two languages across a person, a sign, a school, a valley, a mind, a dictionary and a law.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把两种语言配到人、标牌、学校、山谷、心智、词典与法律之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one sheet folded down the middle, the same sentence on both halves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张从中间对折的纸，两半写着同一句话。

branches.en: THE COUNT: exactly two languages is the word's whole definition.
branches.cn: 数目：正好两种语言，就是这个词的全部定义。

branches.en: THE SPEAKER: a person can carry both languages through a whole life.
branches.cn: 说话者：一个人可以把两种语言带过一生。

branches.en: WORDS ON PAPER: labels and dictionaries put the two side by side.
branches.cn: 纸上的词：标签与词典把两者并排放置。

branches.en: PLACES THAT TEACH: schools and whole valleys keep two languages alive together.
branches.cn: 教学之地：学校与整条山谷让两种语言一同存活。

branches.en: MIND AND LAW: one brain holds both, and one statute can promise both.
branches.cn: 心智与法律：一个头脑容纳两者，一项法规也能承诺两者。

intro.en: The word is two Latin pieces and an English adjective ending, and each piece also builds a family.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个拉丁成分与一个英语形容词词尾构成，每个成分也都构成一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin bis 'twice' supplies the counting prefix, Latin lingua the root, and the adjective ending makes the description; the same pieces build multilingual and monolingual.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 bis「两次」提供计数前缀，拉丁 lingua 提供词根，形容词词尾完成描述；同样的成分也构成「多语的」与「单语的」。

items.example: The prefix fixes the count at exactly two.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把数目固定为二。

items.example: The root names what is counted.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被计数的东西。

items.example: The ending turns the count into a description.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把数目变成描述。

items.example: The bilingual form served both communities.
items.exampleCN: 这份双语表格服务两个社群。

items.example: Bilingualism began at home, not at school.
items.exampleCN: 双语现象始于家庭，而非学校。

items.example: The ceremony was conducted bilingually.
A multilingual city outgrows the pair.
items.exampleCN: 一座多语城市超出了「两种」的范围。

items.example: Monolingual readers needed a translation.

definition_zh: 因循惯例；常规性；对既定习俗与形式的遵从
definition_en: the quality of following established customs, forms and expectations
core_image: 一排排相同的窗、相同的门牌、相同的窗帘长度，街道像照着同一张图纸长出来
scene: 老式婚礼上，长辈坚持按旧顺序敬茶、拍照、入席，年轻人只好照着走。 The wedding followed the conventionality of an older generation, from tea to photographs to seating.
sceneCN: 这里 conventionality 指对既定习俗与程序的遵从（第 1 个义项：按惯例办事的性质）；句意为这场婚礼照着老一辈的惯例，从敬茶、拍照到入席一一照做。

pos.zh: 因循惯例；常规性（不可数，指性质或状态）
具体的惯例言行（用复数 conventionalities，指若干客套做法）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指若干具体惯例）

derivatives.zh: 惯例；会议（由拉丁 conventio「聚在一起、约定」经古法语进入英语，从聚会转指共同约定）
惯例的；因循的（由 convention 加表示「属于」的后缀构成，转指照既定形式办事）
按惯例地（由 conventional 加表示「方式」的后缀构成，转指以惯例为尺度）
不落俗套的（由表示否定的前缀加 conventional 构成，转指脱离既定形式）
召集；集会（由拉丁 convenire「聚到一起」直接借入，保留「走到一处」的动作义）
方便；便利（同出 convenire，由「相合、适配」转指省事合宜）

senses.title: Following accepted customs
senses.definition: the habit or quality of doing things in the way that has long been accepted
senses.definitionCN: 按长期被接受的方式办事的习惯或性质
senses.example: The wedding followed the conventionality of an older generation, from tea to photographs to seating.
senses.exampleCN: 这场婚礼照着老一辈的惯例，从敬茶、拍照到入席一一照做。
senses.why: The word names a quality rather than a single act: it is the tendency to let the accepted order decide the order of events.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是一种性质，而非单个动作：让被接受的次序来决定事件次序的倾向。

senses.title: Being ordinary and unoriginal
senses.definition: the quality of being predictable, unoriginal or unadventurous
senses.definitionCN: 可预测、缺乏原创、不敢冒险的性质
senses.example: Critics complained about the conventionality of the plot, not its craft.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抱怨的是情节的陈旧，而不是技巧。
senses.why: A second judgement attaches to the same quality: following the accepted can look safe or merely dull.
senses.whyCN: 同一种性质还带着第二种评价：照既定路子走，可以显得稳妥，也可以显得乏味。

senses.title: Conventional phrasing or formality
senses.definition: the use of fixed polite phrases and forms rather than fresh or personal expression
senses.definitionCN: 使用固定的礼貌说法与形式，而非新鲜或个人的表达
senses.example: The letter opened with the conventionality of a formal greeting.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信以正式问候的客套话开头。
senses.why: Language has ready-made forms for recurring situations, and their use is itself a kind of social compliance.
senses.whyCN: 语言为反复出现的情境准备了现成形式，使用这些形式本身就是一种社会遵从。

senses.title: Norm-driven social behaviour
senses.titleCN: 由规范驱动的社会行为
senses.definition: behaviour guided by what a group expects rather than by private preference
senses.definitionCN: 由群体期待而非个人偏好引导的行为
senses.example: The conventionality of the neighbourhood kept everyone's curtains the same length.
senses.exampleCN: 街区的因循惯例让每家的窗帘长度都一样。
senses.why: Here the abstract quality becomes visible in a street: shared expectations turn into repeated physical details.
senses.whyCN: 这里抽象性质在街道上显形：共享期待变成重复的物理细节。

senses.title: Adherence to established forms in art
senses.definition: the reliance on established rules, genres or techniques instead of breaking them
senses.definitionCN: 依赖既定规则、体裁或技法，而非打破它们
senses.example: The composer's conventionality made the symphony easy to predict but hard to remember.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作曲家的程式化让交响曲容易预测，却难以记住。
senses.why: Art criticism uses the word to measure how far a work stays inside the rules of its genre.
senses.whyCN: 艺术批评用这个词衡量一件作品在多大程度上留在其体裁规则之内。

senses.title: Mere formality without substance
senses.definition: the state of keeping up a ceremony or courtesy after its meaning has gone
senses.definitionCN: 意义消失后仍维持仪式或礼节的状况
senses.example: The committee's conventionality produced minutes but no decision.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会的例行程序产出了会议记录，却没有决定。
senses.why: When form outlives purpose, the same word turns from praise to complaint: it now means hollow compliance.
senses.whyCN: 当形式活得比目的更久，同一个词就从称赞变成抱怨：它现在指空洞的遵从。

senses.title: Compliance as social lubricant
senses.definition: the everyday compliance that lets strangers act together without negotiating every step
senses.definitionCN: 让陌生人不必逐步协商也能共同行动的日常遵从
senses.example: A little conventionality lets a crowded train load without argument.
senses.exampleCN: 一点因循惯例让拥挤的列车不吵不闹地装满人。
senses.why: The quality is not only a constraint; it is also the grease that saves everyone from explaining themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这种性质不只是约束，也是省去人人自我解释的润滑剂。

senses.title: Abstract: predictability through shared rules
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：共享规则带来的可预期性
senses.definition: the predictability that arises when many people follow the same unwritten rules
senses.definitionCN: 许多人遵守同一套不成文规则时产生的可预期性
senses.example: Markets rely on the conventionality of strangers more than on written contracts.
senses.exampleCN: 市场依赖陌生人的惯例，胜过依赖书面合同。
senses.why: At its most abstract the word names the reliability that shared rules create, apart from any single rule.
senses.whyCN: 推到最抽象处，这个词命名的是共享规则造成的可靠性，与任何单条规则无关。

intro.en: Conventionality is convention plus two suffixes. Convention comes from Latin conventio, 'a meeting, an agreement', built on convenire 'to come together'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: conventionality 是 convention 加两层后缀构成。convention 来自拉丁 conventio「聚会、约定」，其动词 convenire 意为「走到一起」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Venire meant 'to come'. It is the base of many English words about arriving, assembling or intervening.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」。它是许多表示到达、聚集或介入的英语词的基底。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus venire produced convenire 'to come together, assemble, agree'.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的成分加 venire 构成 convenire「走到一起、集会、达成一致」。

items.en: Conventio named a meeting or an agreement, and from 'what has been agreed' came the sense of an accepted practice.
items.cn: conventio 指聚会或约定，又从「已经商定之事」引申出「被接受的做法」。

items.en: Old French convention carried the word into English, where convention first meant an assembly and later a accepted custom.
items.cn: 古法语 convention 把这个词带进英语，convention 最初指集会，后来指被接受的习俗。

items.en: Conventional added an adjective ending to convention; conventionality then added a suffix of quality, naming the state of being conventional.
items.cn: conventional 由 convention 加形容词词尾构成；conventionality 再加表示性质的后缀，命名「因循」这一状态。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first printed use of conventionality is not recorded, though it is generally dated to the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：conventionality 最早印行于何时没有记录，一般认为在十七世纪。

note.en: Group one holds the same Latin 'come together' family plus one look-alike from a different root; group two holds words for social compliance.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「走到一起」词族的词，外加一个异源形近词；第二组是表示社会遵从的词。

entries.definition: The accepted practice or formal assembly; conventionality is the quality of following such practices.
entries.definitionCN: 被接受的做法或正式会议；conventionality 是遵从这类做法的性质。

entries.definition: Describing something that follows convention; the noun names the quality behind that description.
entries.definitionCN: 形容照惯例行事的事物；名词则命名这一形容背后的性质。

entries.definition: Also from convenire, but it means ease or suitability, not adherence to custom.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 convenire，却指方便或合宜，而非对习俗的遵从。

entries.definition: From Latin vincere 'to conquer', not venire. It means a firm belief or a court finding, with no custom sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 vincere「征服」，并非 venire；它指坚定信念或法庭判定，没有习俗义。

entries.definition: Behaviour that matches the group; it stresses what people do, while conventionality stresses the established forms they follow.
entries.definitionCN: 与群体一致的行为；它强调人做什么，而 conventionality 强调人所遵循的既定形式。

entries.definition: Strict adherence to an approved doctrine, usually religious or political; it is stronger and more doctrinal.
entries.definitionCN: 对获准教义的严格遵守，通常指宗教或政治；语气更强，也更教条。

entries.definition: The quality of being formal or ceremonial; it can exist without the wider social custom that conventionality names.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或合乎礼仪的性质；它可以不带 conventionality 所指的更广社会习俗。

entries.definition: A handed-down way of doing something; conventionality is the disposition to keep to such ways.
entries.definitionCN: 世代沿袭的做法；conventionality 是守着这类做法的倾向。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定说法与真实的同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Convenir means come together, so a convention is first a gathering, then what the gathering agrees on.
normal.cn: convenire 意为走到一起，所以 convention 先是聚会，再是聚会商定之事。

normal.en: Conventionality adds a suffix of quality, turning the practice into a disposition.
normal.cn: conventionality 加一层表示性质的后缀，把做法变成倾向。

normal.en: Fixed phrases test the tone: strict conventionality, mere conventionality, break with conventionality.
normal.cn: 固定说法试出语气：严格因循、仅仅是客套、打破惯例。

normal.en: Convenience shares the same root but means ease, not compliance, so the two must not be swapped.
normal.cn: convenience 同根却指方便，不指遵从，二者不可互换。

normal.en: The adjective is conventional and the adverb conventionally; the noun keeps the abstract quality.
normal.cn: 形容词是 conventional，副词是 conventionally，名词保留抽象性质。

abstract.en: Picture a street where every curtain stops at the same height, though no rule says so.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街，家家窗帘都停在同样的高度，却没有任何规则这样要求。

abstract.en: Picture a wedding rehearsal where every step has a fixed order and a fixed phrase.
abstract.cn: 想象一场婚礼排练，每一步都有固定次序与固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that runs smoothly only because every part repeats the same motion.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器之所以顺畅，只因为每个部件重复同一个动作。

examples.en: The architect's conventionality made the building easy to approve and hard to love.
examples.cn: 这位建筑师的因循让方案容易获批，却难以让人喜爱。

examples.en: A little conventionality keeps a shared office peaceful.
examples.cn: 一点因循惯例能让共享办公室保持平静。

examples.en: The novel mocks the conventionality of its own ending.
examples.cn: 这部小说嘲讽自己结局的程式化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康文 申 那里提」——大家走到一起商定下来的老规矩 → 因循惯例

root: 拉丁 convenire「走到一起、达成一致」+ 拉丁 conventio「聚会、约定」；后加表示性质的拉丁后缀构成，一般认为十七世纪出现于英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat the quality as a disposition to keep to accepted forms, then show it as dullness, fixed phrasing, street-level repetition, artistic rule-keeping, hollow ceremony, social lubrication and finally predictability itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先把这个性质看作守着既定形式的倾向，再依次显示为陈旧、程式化说法、街道层面的重复、艺术上的守规、空洞仪式、社交润滑，最后是可预期性本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a street built from one drawing, every window and curtain repeating the same measurement.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条照着同一张图纸建成的街，每扇窗、每幅窗帘都重复同一个尺寸。

branches.en: THE DISPOSITION AND ITS STREET: a habit of following accepted order, visible in repeated physical details.
branches.cn: 倾向与它的街道：遵从既定次序的习惯，显形为重复的物理细节。

branches.en: SAFE OR DULL: the same quality read as unoriginality, and as reliance on established artistic forms.
branches.cn: 稳妥或乏味：同一性质既被读作陈旧，也被读作依赖既定艺术形式。

branches.en: FORM WITHOUT SPIRIT: fixed polite phrasing, then ceremony kept up after its meaning has gone.
branches.cn: 有形式无精神：先是固定客套话，再是意义消失后仍维持的仪式。

branches.en: SOCIAL LUBRICANT: compliance saves strangers from negotiating every step.
branches.cn: 社交润滑：遵从让陌生人省去逐步协商。

branches.en: PREDICTABILITY: the widest reading names the reliability shared rules create.
branches.cn: 可预期性：最宽的读法命名共享规则造成的可靠性。

intro.en: Conventionality is a Latin verb, a noun of agreement and two English suffixes stacked on one stem.
intro.cn: conventionality 是一个拉丁动词、一个表示约定的名词，再在同一个词干上叠两层英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin venire gives convene, convention, convenient, intervene and prevent; the same stem builds conventionality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 venire 衍生 convene、convention、convenient、intervene 与 prevent；同一词干还构成 conventionality。

items.exampleCN: conventio 把聚集变成已定之事。

items.example: Convention moved from meeting to custom.

items.example: The noun names the disposition itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名倾向本身。

items.example: The negative shows how strong the expectation is.
items.exampleCN: 否定形式显示这种期待有多强。

items.exampleCN: convenience 保留词根里「相合」的一面。
