definition_zh: 领土的；领地的；地盘性的；区域性的
definition_en: relating to territory, especially to land held by a state or to an area defended by an animal or person
core_image: 地图上的国界线与动物在草丛中留下的一圈气味线叠在一起
scene: 两只雄鸟在河岸的柳丛间追逐，驱赶靠近边界的同类。 Two male birds chased each other through the riverside willows, driving away rivals that came near the territorial boundary.
sceneCN: 这里 territorial 是「地盘性的、防卫领域的」（第 2 个义项：动物对领域的防卫）；句意：两只雄鸟在河岸柳丛间互相追逐，把靠近领地边界的同类赶走。

pos.zh: 领土的；领地的；地盘性的；区域性的
领土防卫军成员（英国用法，Territorial）

senses.title: Relating to a state's land
senses.definition: concerning the land and waters governed by a state
senses.definitionCN: 涉及国家治理的陆地与水域
senses.example: The two countries signed a territorial agreement over the island.
senses.exampleCN: 两国就该岛签署了一项领土协议。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches territory's political sense to a noun: whatever is territorial concerns land held under a state's authority.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把 territory 的政治义附加到名词上：凡是 territorial 的，都涉及国家权力下的土地。

senses.title: Defending an area, in animals
senses.definition: describing an animal that defends a fixed area against rivals
senses.definitionCN: 描述动物防卫固定区域、抵御同类的行为
senses.example: Territorial males sing to keep rivals away from the nest site.
senses.exampleCN: 有领域性的雄鸟鸣唱，使竞争者远离巢址。
senses.why: Ethology borrowed the political adjective: the bird behaves as if it holds title to a patch, and its song is the boundary notice.
senses.whyCN: 动物行为学借用了这个政治形容词：鸟表现得仿佛对一块地拥有产权，鸣唱就是边界通告。

senses.title: Of waters claimed by a state
senses.definition: relating to the belt of sea over which a coastal state claims jurisdiction
senses.definitionCN: 与沿海国主张管辖的带状海域有关
senses.example: Foreign ships must respect the territorial waters of the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 外国船只必须尊重沿海国的领海。
senses.why: Water is treated like land for legal purpose: the same adjective extends the state's boundary from soil to sea, producing 'territorial waters'.
senses.whyCN: 法律上把水当作土地处理：同一形容词把国家边界从陆地延伸到海洋，形成 territorial waters。

senses.title: Of claims, disputes, and integrity
senses.titleCN: 关于领土主张、争端与完整
senses.definition: concerning demands over land, conflicts about boundaries, or the principle that a state's land must not be broken up
senses.definitionCN: 涉及对土地的要求、边界冲突，或国家领土不可分割的原则
senses.example: Territorial integrity is written into the charter.
senses.exampleCN: 领土完整被写入宪章。
senses.why: Once land is bounded, it can be claimed, disputed, or guaranteed. The adjective names the legal and diplomatic dimension of those boundaries.
senses.whyCN: 土地一旦有边界，就可以被主张、争夺或保障。该形容词命名这些边界的法律与外交维度。

senses.title: Organized by region
senses.definition: divided or administered according to regional areas rather than a single centre
senses.definitionCN: 按区域划分或管理，而非由单一中心统管
senses.example: The agency adopted a territorial structure with six regional offices.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构采用按区域划分的结构，设六个地区办事处。
senses.why: The noun's 'district' sense becomes an administrative adjective: an organization mirrors a map, and each unit governs its own patch.
senses.whyCN: 名词的“区域”义转为行政形容词：组织像地图一样被划分，每个单元管理自己的一块。

senses.title: Possessive about personal space
senses.titleCN: 对个人空间有地盘意识的
senses.definition: in everyday use, describing a person who treats a place or role as exclusively theirs
senses.definitionCN: 日常用法中描述把某处或某角色视为专属的人
senses.example: He gets territorial about his desk when interns borrow it.
senses.exampleCN: 实习生借用他的桌子时，他就很有地盘意识。
senses.why: Human behaviour is described with the animal adjective: the desk is not legally owned in the relevant sense, but it is defended like a range.
senses.whyCN: 用动物的形容词描述人类行为：那张桌子在相关意义上并非法律所有，却像领地一样被防卫。

senses.title: Of a local defence force
senses.definition: in British usage, relating to the volunteer reserve army organized by region
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法中，与按地区组织的志愿预备役部队有关
senses.example: He served in the Territorial Army for eight years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在地方防卫军服役八年。
senses.why: The word's 'regional' sense explains the name: a force raised and organized by locality rather than as a standing national army.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的“区域”义解释了名称：按地方征募与组织的部队，而不是常备国家军队。

senses.title: Of animal space use in ecology
senses.titleCN: 生态学中关于空间利用的
senses.definition: in ecology, describing systems where individuals or groups exclude others from an area
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中描述个体或群体排斥他者进入某区域的体系
senses.example: Territorial species often show stable population densities.
senses.exampleCN: 领域性物种常表现出稳定的种群密度。
senses.why: Ecology turns the adjective into a technical classifier: a species is territorial if its spacing is maintained by exclusion rather than by random movement.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把这个形容词变成技术分类：若某物种的间距靠排斥而非随机移动维持，它就是 territorial。

intro.en: Territorial is the English adjective from territory, formed with -ial. Its base is Latin terra 'land'; the disputed terrere 'frighten' link belongs to the noun's uncertain fringe.
intro.cn: territorial 是由 territory 加 -ial 构成的英语形容词。词基是拉丁语 terra「土地」；有争议的 terrere「使恐惧」联系属于名词的不确定边缘。

items.en: The adjective territorial is recorded in the eighteenth century, derived from territory rather than borrowed as a ready-made Latin adjective.
items.cn: 形容词 territorial 于 18 世纪被记录，由 territory 派生，而不是直接借入现成的拉丁形容词。

items.en: territory < territorium 'land around a town' < terra 'earth, land'. The adjective therefore means 'of the land belonging to a centre'.
items.cn: territory < territorium「城镇周围的土地」< terra「土地」。因此形容词意为“属于某一中心的土地的”。

items.en: The alternative derivation from terrere 'to frighten' is sometimes repeated for territory; it is not settled, so the 'land kept by fear' nuance is source uncertain.
items.cn: 另有把 territory 追溯到 terrere「使恐惧」的说法常被重复，但并无定论，故“靠恐惧守住的土地”这一层含义来源不确定。

items.en: The adjective extended to territorial waters and territorial integrity in international law, and to territorial behaviour in zoology.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，该形容词扩展到国际法中的领海与领土完整，以及动物学中的领域行为。

items.en: Modern usage distinguishes territory (the area) from territorial (the relation to it); the noun territorial is chiefly British and refers to a reservist.
items.cn: 现代用法区分 territory（区域）与 territorial（与之相关）；名词 territorial 主要为英式用法，指预备役军人。

note.en: The first group separates spelling relatives, the second compares adjectives of land and defence.
note.cn: 第一组区分拼写同族词，第二组比较表示土地与防卫的形容词。

entries.definition: the area itself; the adjective describes what relates to it.
entries.definitionCN: 区域本身；形容词描述与它相关的事物。

entries.definition: of the earth or land, often opposed to aquatic or celestial. It shares terra but not the political boundary sense.
entries.definitionCN: 地球的或陆生的，常与水生或天体相对。共享 terra，但无政治边界义。

entries.definition: the physical surface of land; terrain is ground as shape, territory is ground as claim.
entries.definitionCN: 土地的地表形态；terrain 是形状意义上的地面，territory 是主张意义上的地面。

entries.definition: extreme fear, from terrere. Its connection to territory is only the disputed hypothesis.
entries.definitionCN: 极度恐惧，来自 terrere。它与 territory 的联系仅是存疑假设。

entries.definition: relating to a region; it lacks the legal claim and defence senses of territorial.
entries.definitionCN: 与区域有关的；缺少 territorial 的法律主张与防卫义。

entries.definition: wanting to keep what one has; in everyday use it overlaps with territorial about space.
entries.definitionCN: 想要保住自己所有的；日常用法中在空间问题上与 territorial 重叠。

entries.definition: acting to protect against attack; territorial behaviour is often defensive but not always.
entries.definitionCN: 为防攻击而行动；领域行为常是防御性的，但不总是。

entries.definition: relating to the power to govern an area; it stresses authority rather than boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 与治理某区域的权力有关；强调权威而非边界。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffix patterns and standard legal and biological phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀模式与法律、生物学的标准搭配。

normal.en: territory + -ial makes the adjective; anything territorial 'belongs to' a territory.
normal.cn: territory + -ial 构成形容词；territorial 的东西“属于”某个 territory。

normal.en: Territorial waters extends land law to a belt of sea.
normal.cn: territorial waters 把土地法延伸到一条海域。

normal.en: Territorial integrity is the legal phrase for 'the land must not be broken up'.
normal.cn: territorial integrity 是“领土不可被分割”的法律用语。

normal.en: Territorial behaviour is the ethology phrase for animals excluding rivals from a patch.
normal.cn: territorial behaviour 是动物行为学中“把竞争者排除在某块地”的用语。

normal.en: The British Territorial Army is regional by design; the adjective's 'regional' sense names it.
normal.cn: 英国 Territorial Army 按地区组织；形容词的“区域”义正是其名称来源。

abstract.en: Picture a fence: the land is territory, the fence's logic is territorial, and the habit of guarding it is territoriality.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆：土地是 territory，篱笆的逻辑是 territorial，守卫它的习性则是 territoriality。

abstract.en: The same adjective covers state borders and a desk at work because both are areas a holder excludes others from.
abstract.cn: 同一形容词覆盖国界与办公桌，因为两者都是持有者排斥他人的区域。

abstract.en: Territorial is relational: it never names the land alone, only the land seen through a claim.
abstract.cn: territorial 是关系性的：它从不单独命名土地，只命名透过“主张”看到的土地。

examples.en: The dispute over territorial waters has lasted for decades.
examples.cn: 关于领海的争端已持续数十年。

examples.en: Territorial birds attack intruders much larger than themselves.
examples.cn: 领域性鸟类会攻击比自己大得多的入侵者。

examples.en: She became territorial about the project after working on it alone.
examples.cn: 独自做了一段时间后，她对这个项目有了地盘意识。

dict_mnemonic.text: “特瑞托瑞尔”——特别划定的一块地里，谁进来就赶谁 → territorial 领土的、地盘性的

root: 由 territory 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成；territory 出自拉丁语 territorium（terra「土地」）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of territorial: the adjective follows territory from state land to defended animal space, administrative regions, personal space, reserve forces, and ecological spacing.
sensesIntro.cn: territorial 的八个义项：这个形容词随 territory 从国家土地延伸到动物防卫空间、行政区域、个人空间、预备役部队与生态间距。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary line, whether a national border or a scent mark in grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条边界线，无论是国界还是草丛中的气味标记。

branches.en: LAND AND CLAIMS: the state's own ground and the claims made about it are one boundary question seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 土地与主张：国家自己的土地与围绕它提出的主张，是同一个边界问题从两面看的样子。

branches.en: SEA: waters a state claims carry the land boundary outward onto the water.
branches.cn: 海域：国家主张的海域把陆地边界向外延伸到水上。

branches.en: ANIMAL SPACING: defence of an area produces regular distances between individuals.
branches.cn: 动物间距：对区域的防卫使个体之间形成规则的距离。

branches.en: ADMINISTRATION: regional offices and local defence forces mirror the map.
branches.cn: 行政与防卫：地区机构与地方防卫力量是地图在组织上的对应物。

branches.en: PERSONAL SPACE: a desk, a seat, or a role is defended as if it were land.
branches.cn: 个人空间：一张桌子、一个座位或一个角色，也会像土地一样被防卫。

intro.en: Territorial is territory plus the Latin-derived adjective suffix -ial. The suffix is productive in English (editorial, residential), but the base is a borrowed noun.
intro.cn: territorial 是 territory 加拉丁来源的形容词后缀 -ial。该后缀在英语中能产（editorial、residential），但词基是借入的名词。

latinIntro.en: The terra family supplies territory, terrain, terrace, terracotta, and Mediterranean; the -ial suffix also builds memorial, financial, and substantial.
latinIntro.cn: terra 一族提供 territory、terrain、terrace、terracotta、Mediterranean；-ial 后缀还构成 memorial、financial、substantial。

items.meaningCN: 与领土有关的（-ial 形容词）
items.example: Territorial claims are sensitive.
The sea is territorially divided.
items.exampleCN: 这片海在领土上被划分。

items.meaningCN: 领域性；属地性（-ity 名词）
items.example: Territoriality regulates spacing.
The state territorialized the coast.

items.meaning: a bounded area held by someone
items.meaningCN: 被某方持有的有界区域
items.example: The territory is rich in minerals.
The terrain rises sharply.
The terrace holds rainwater.
Terrestrial animals breathe air.

latinEntries.meaningCN: 使恐惧（与 territory 的联系存疑）

definition_zh: 压迫；不义的统治或制度性压制；沉重压抑的感受
definition_en: the unjust or cruel exercise of power over a group, or the heavy sense of being weighed down
core_image: 一盘沉重的石磨压在一排肩上，磨盘下的地面被压出深深的凹痕
scene: 工厂门口，工人排成长队等候检查，守卫把证件扔回他们脸上，午后的热气压在低矮的屋顶下。 The novel describes the oppression, the unjust weight of rule that kept the whole district silent.
sceneCN: 这里 oppression 指「制度性的不义压制」（第 1 个义项：长期施于群体的沉重统治）；句意为小说描写了让整个街区噤声的那种压迫。可辨识物件：工厂门、长队、证件、守卫、低矮屋顶下的热气。

pos.zh: 压迫；压制；压抑感（可数，复数 oppressions）

senses.title: Systematic unjust rule over a group
senses.titleCN: 对群体的系统性不义统治
senses.definition: the prolonged, unjust exercise of power that keeps a group down
senses.definitionCN: 长期不义地行使权力，使一个群体处于低下地位
senses.example: The novel describes the oppression that kept the whole district silent.
senses.exampleCN: 小说描写了让整个街区噤声的那种压迫。
senses.why: opprimere is ob- 'against' plus premere 'press': power is pressed down on someone until they cannot rise.
senses.whyCN: opprimere 是 ob-「对着」加 premere「压」：权力压在某人身上，直到他起不来。

senses.title: A heavy feeling of being weighed down
senses.definition: a bodily or mental sense of heaviness, tightness or suffocation
senses.definitionCN: 身体或心理上沉重、紧绷或窒息的感受
senses.example: A sudden oppression in the chest made him sit down.
senses.exampleCN: 胸口突然一阵压抑，使他坐了下来。
senses.why: the physical image of pressing explains the feeling: something invisible sits on the breath.
senses.whyCN: 「压」的身体意象解释了这种感受：有某种无形之物压住了呼吸。

senses.title: A specific oppressive act or measure
senses.titleCN: 具体的压迫行为或措施
senses.definition: one law, order or action that imposes unjust burden on people
senses.definitionCN: 给人们施加不义负担的一项法律、命令或行动
senses.example: Each oppression was recorded in the parish ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次压迫都被记在教区账簿里。
senses.why: a system is made of measures, and the countable plural names them one by one.
senses.whyCN: 制度由措施构成，可数复数把它们逐条命名。

senses.title: Economic oppression
senses.definition: exploitative wages, debt, rents or exclusion that keep people poor by design
senses.definitionCN: 有意使人贫穷的剥削性工资、债务、租金或排斥
senses.example: Debt peonage was an economic oppression dressed as contract.
senses.exampleCN: 债务劳役是披着契约外衣的经济压迫。
senses.why: pressure can be applied through prices and contracts, not only through police.
senses.whyCN: 压力可以通过价格与契约施加，而不只是通过警察。

senses.title: Gender or ethnic oppression
senses.definition: structural disadvantage imposed on people because of gender, caste, ethnicity or similar identity
senses.definitionCN: 因性别、种姓、族群等身份而强加的结构性劣势
senses.example: The report documented the oppression of migrant women.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了对移民女性的压迫。
senses.why: the same heavy hand can target a category rather than an individual, which is why the word pairs with identity terms.
senses.whyCN: 同一只重手可以针对一个类别而非个人，因此这个词常与身份词搭配。

senses.title: A historical oppressive regime
senses.definition: a named colonial, caste or authoritarian order studied as a system
senses.definitionCN: 被作为制度研究的殖民、种姓或专制秩序
senses.example: Scholars compare the oppression of two colonial administrations.
senses.exampleCN: 学者比较两套殖民行政的压迫方式。
senses.why: historians treat oppression as an institutional design, not only as individual cruelty.
senses.whyCN: 历史学家把压迫当作制度设计，而不只是个人残忍。

senses.title: Metaphor: psychological or environmental weight
senses.titleCN: 比喻：心理或环境的重压
senses.definition: by extension, any atmosphere or mood that makes people feel small and tired
senses.definitionCN: 引申指任何使人感到渺小而疲惫的气氛或情绪
senses.example: A grey sky added its own oppression to the afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 灰暗的天空给这个下午添了一层自己的压抑。
senses.why: the metaphor transfers the stone's weight to air, light and mood.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把石头的重量转移到空气、光线与情绪上。

senses.title: Abstraction: any force that contracts freedom
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：收缩自由的力量
senses.definition: any structure or pressure that narrows a person's or group's room to act
senses.definitionCN: 任何缩小个人或群体行动空间的结构或压力
senses.example: Oppression is freedom compressed until it cannot breathe.
senses.exampleCN: 压迫是被压缩到无法呼吸的自由。
senses.why: the deepest sense is spatial: the hand does not only hurt, it reduces the space in which one can move.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是空间性的：那只手不仅造成疼痛，还缩小了可行动的空间。

intro.en: Oppression comes from Latin opprimere, ob- 'against' plus premere 'to press'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oppression 来自拉丁 opprimere，由 ob-「对着」与 premere「压」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Opprimere meant 'to press against, crush, overwhelm', built from ob- 'against, toward' and premere 'to press'.
items.cn: opprimere 意为「压向、压碎、压倒」，由 ob-「对着、朝向」与 premere「压」构成。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press, squeeze'; its deeper origin is usually reconstructed with a root for striking, a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: premere 意为「压、挤」；其更深来源通常以一个表示「击打」的词根重构，属重构而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Oppressio named a pressing down or crushing; the noun carried the physical weight of the verb into abstract use.
items.cn: oppressio 指压下或压碎；这个名词把动词的身体重量带入抽象用法。

items.en: Oppression entered English through Old French in the fourteenth century, first as a general word for crushing or burden.
items.cn: oppression 在十四世纪经古法语进入英语，最初泛指压碎或重负。

items.en: The political sense of unjust rule took shape in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries and dominates modern usage.
items.cn: 不义统治的政治义在十七、十八世纪成形，并主导现代用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (political sense date and root shape): the exact point at which the word became primarily political is not fixed, and the pre-Latin root of premere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（政治义年代与词根形态）：这个词何时主要转为政治义并无定论，premere 的拉丁语前词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds press-root words that are easily swapped with oppression; group two holds neighbouring ideas of unjust power.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「压」词根、易与 oppression 互换的词；第二组是不义权力的邻近概念。

entries.definition: From sub- 'down' plus premere: the act of putting something down by force, such as a revolt or a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 sub-「向下」加 premere：以武力压下某物，如叛乱或事实。

entries.definition: From re- 'back' plus premere: keeping something from emerging, often used for impulses or dissent.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 re-「向后」加 premere：阻止某物浮现，常用于冲动或异议。

entries.definition: From de- 'down' plus premere: a lowered state, whether of ground, economy or mood. It is not a political term.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 de-「向下」加 premere：被压低的状态，可为地面、经济或情绪，并非政治术语。

entries.definition: From com- 'together' plus premere: squeezing into less space, a physical rather than social process.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 com-「一起」加 premere：压进更小空间，是物理过程而非社会过程。

entries.definition: Cruel and arbitrary rule by one person or a small clique; oppression can be impersonal and institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 指一人或小集团的残暴专断统治；oppression 可以是非个人的、制度性的。

entries.definition: Taking advantage of people's labour or weakness for profit; it is one engine of economic oppression.
entries.definitionCN: 指利用他人劳动或弱点获利；它是经济压迫的一种引擎。

entries.definition: Treating people differently because of identity; it can occur without a heavy system of rule.
entries.definitionCN: 指因身份而区别对待；可以没有沉重的统治体系。

entries.definition: The act of conquering and subjecting a people; it stresses the moment of defeat more than daily pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指征服并使一个民族臣服；更强调被击败的时刻，而非日常压力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin pieces, the press-root family and the bodily image of weight.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁成分、press 词根家族，以及「重量」的身体意象。

normal.en: ob- 'against' + premere 'press': a hand pressing against someone until they cannot stand.
normal.cn: ob-「对着」+ premere「压」：一只手压在人身上，直到他站不起来。

normal.en: The family runs press, pressure, compress, suppress, repress, depress, oppress.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 press、pressure、compress、suppress、repress、depress、oppress。

normal.en: The prefixes show direction: sub- down, re- back, de- down, com- together, ob- against.
normal.cn: 前缀显示方向：sub- 向下、re- 向后、de- 向下、com- 一起、ob- 对着。

normal.en: Oppression has both a political sense and a bodily sense of heavy breathing.
normal.cn: oppression 既有政治义，也有呼吸沉重的身体义。

normal.en: Typical partners are live under, escape, systematic and economic.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「生活在……之下」「逃离」「系统性的」与「经济的」。

abstract.en: Picture a stone lid placed over a pot so that nothing can rise out.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石板盖住锅口，使任何东西都升不出来。

abstract.en: Picture a room whose walls move inward a little each year.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间，墙壁每年向内挪一点。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that weighs a person every morning and never lets the needle fall.
abstract.cn: 想象一台每天早上称人的秤，指针从不肯下落。

examples.en: The characters speak quietly because oppression has taught them caution.
examples.cn: 人物说话很轻，因为压迫教会了他们谨慎。

examples.en: Economic oppression can outlast the laws that created it.
examples.cn: 经济压迫可能比造成它的法律活得更久。

examples.en: The painting conveys the oppression of a low ceiling and a grey light.
examples.cn: 这幅画传达了低矮天花板与灰光的压抑感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「op（对着）+ press（压）」——一直对着人往下压 → 压迫

root: 拉丁 opprimere「压向、压倒」= ob-（对着）+ premere（压）；名词 oppressio。premere 的更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one gesture: a weight is pressed down. The weight becomes a political system, then a bodily feeling, then single measures, then economic and identity-based forms, then a historical regime, then a mood and finally any narrowing of freedom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个动作展开：把重量压下去。这个重量先成为政治制度，再成为身体感受，再成为单项措施，再成为经济与身份形式，再成为历史政权，再成为气氛，最后成为对自由的任何收窄。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a millstone resting on a row of shoulders, the ground dented beneath it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盘石磨压在一排肩上，地面被压出凹痕。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM AND ITS MEASURES: rule is applied one order at a time.
branches.cn: 制度与措施：统治是按一条条命令施加的。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT FELT: the stone becomes breath, sky and mood.
branches.cn: 感到的重量：石头变成呼吸、天空与情绪。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL AND THE CATEGORY: money and identity are two faces of the same hand.
branches.cn: 物质与类别：金钱与身份是同一只手的两个面。

branches.en: THE REGIME: historians study oppression as an institutional design.
branches.cn: 政权：历史学家把压迫当作制度设计来研究。

branches.en: THE SHRUNKEN ROOM: the deepest sense is reduced space for action.
branches.cn: 收缩的房间：最深的一层是行动空间的缩小。

intro.en: Oppression is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb root, and the same root builds a whole family of pressing words in English.
intro.cn: oppression 是拉丁前缀加拉丁动词词根，同一词根在英语中构成整个「压」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere gives press, pressure, compress, suppress, repress and depress; ob- adds the sense of pressing against.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 premere 衍生 press、pressure、compress、suppress、repress 与 depress；ob- 增添「对着压」的意思。

items.example: The prefix gives the pressure a direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给压力一个方向。

items.example: The root is the physical act of pressing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是「压」这个身体动作。

items.example: The Latin verb joined direction and weight.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词把方向与重量结合起来。

items.example: Oppression can be a policy, not only a temper.
items.exampleCN: 压迫可以是一项政策，而不只是脾气。

items.example: The rules oppressed the poorest tenants.
items.exampleCN: 这些规则压制了最贫穷的佃户。

items.example: The oppressor feared the square at noon.
items.exampleCN: 压迫者害怕正午的广场。

items.example: The heat was oppressive by ten o'clock.
items.exampleCN: 到十点，热气已经令人窒息。

items.example: Press the seal into the wax.
The officers suppressed the protest.
She repressed the urge to answer.

definition_zh: 尖顶；顶峰；极点；浪尖
definition_en: the highest point of a building, a rock, a career or a wave
core_image: 一座石塔最上面那个细尖，风只能从它旁边绕过去
scene: 他四十五岁那年坐上公司最高一层，别人说这就是顶峰。 At forty-five he took the top floor of the firm, and everyone said he had reached the pinnacle.
sceneCN: 这里 pinnacle 指事业的顶峰（第 3 个义项：事业顶峰）；句意为他在四十五岁那年坐上公司最高一层，人人都说他已到顶峰。

pos.zh: 尖顶；顶峰；极点；浪尖

senses.title: Architectural pinnacle
senses.definition: a small pointed ornament on a roof, a tower or a buttress
senses.definitionCN: 屋顶、塔身或扶壁上的小尖状装饰
senses.example: Each pinnacle of the chapel carried a carved saint.
senses.exampleCN: 礼拜堂的每个尖顶上都雕着一位圣人。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, and it is still the most exact.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，也仍是最精确的一个。

senses.title: Rocky point
senses.definition: a sharp point of rock standing above a ridge
senses.definitionCN: 山脊之上凸起的一块尖锐岩石
senses.example: The last pinnacle could be climbed only on a rope.
senses.exampleCN: 最后那座岩峰只能靠绳索攀上去。
senses.why: Stone and stone ornament share a shape, so the word carried over easily.
senses.whyCN: 岩石与石饰共享同一个形状，词就这样轻易地移了过去。

senses.title: Career peak
senses.definition: the highest point that a working life reaches
senses.definitionCN: 职业生涯所达到的最高处
senses.example: She reached the pinnacle of her profession at fifty.
senses.exampleCN: 她在五十岁到达本行的顶峰。
senses.why: Careers are imagined as mountains, which is why the word fits.
senses.whyCN: 事业被想象成山，所以这个词合用。

senses.title: Peak of achievement
senses.definition: the best result a skill or an art has produced so far
senses.definitionCN: 一门技艺或艺术迄今产生的最好结果
senses.example: That quartet remains the pinnacle of his chamber music.
senses.exampleCN: 那首四重奏至今仍是他室内乐的顶点。
senses.why: The word ranks works, not only people.
senses.whyCN: 这个词给作品排名，不只给人排名。

senses.title: Pinnacle of fashion
senses.definition: the moment when a style is most admired
senses.definitionCN: 一种风格最受推崇的那一刻
senses.example: The narrow silhouette was the pinnacle of fashion that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那一年窄身廓形正是时尚之巅。
senses.why: Taste also builds peaks, and it moves them every season.
senses.whyCN: 品味也会堆出山峰，而且每季挪动一次。

senses.title: Social pinnacle
senses.definition: the top of a social order, seen as a place where one stands
senses.definitionCN: 社会秩序的最高处，被看作可以站上去的位置
senses.example: The family had climbed to the pinnacle of local society.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人已爬到本地社会的顶层。
senses.why: Here the height is a rank, not a rock.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「高」是等级，不是岩石。

senses.title: Final point
senses.definition: the last and highest point of a rise, after which comes the descent
senses.definitionCN: 上升过程中最后也是最高的一点，之后就是下降
senses.example: The road reached its pinnacle above the tree line.
senses.exampleCN: 路在树线以上到达最高点。
senses.why: The word names a turning point as well as a height.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既命名高度，也命名转折点。

senses.title: Wave crest
senses.definition: the top of a wave, where a surfer tries to stand
senses.definitionCN: 波浪的最高处，冲浪者想站上去的地方
senses.example: He held the board on the pinnacle for a full second.
senses.exampleCN: 他在浪尖上把板稳住了整整一秒。
senses.why: Water makes a temporary pinnacle, and the word grants it the same honour.
senses.whyCN: 水造出临时的峰顶，词也给它同样的尊称。

intro.en: Pinnacle began as a little feather: Latin pinna meant 'wing', and its diminutive named a small point.
intro.cn: pinnacle 起初是一根小羽毛：拉丁语 pinna 指「翼」，它的指小形式命名了一个小尖。

items.en: Pinna meant 'feather or wing', and also named the feather-shaped parts of a building.
items.cn: pinna 意为「羽毛或翼」，也用来称建筑上羽状的部件。

items.en: The diminutive pinnaculum meant 'a small point or peak'.
items.cn: 指小形式 pinnaculum 意为「小尖、小峰」。

items.en: Old French took the word as pinacle and kept the architectural sense.
items.cn: 古法语把它接作 pinacle，保留了建筑义。

items.en: English borrowed pinacle for the ornament on a roof or a buttress.
items.cn: 英语借入 pinacle，指屋顶或扶壁上的装饰尖。

items.en: Later the word climbed: careers, styles and even waves acquired pinnacles.
items.cn: 后来这个词往上爬：事业、风格甚至波浪都有了 pinnacle。

note.en: The look-alike group is the pinna family; the near-meaning group separates summit, apex, zenith and peak.
note.cn: 形近组是 pinna 词族；近义组把「山顶」「顶点」「天顶」与「高峰」分开。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of the thin stone point that the wind has to go around.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「风只能绕着走的那根细石尖」的画面。

normal.en: Pinnacle holds pinna, Latin for feather: a small pointed thing, light and sharp.
normal.cn: pinnacle 里藏着 pinna（拉丁语的羽毛）：一个小小的尖物，轻而尖。

normal.en: Think of a chapel roof: every corner finishes in a carved point.
normal.cn: 想象礼拜堂的屋顶：每个转角都收成一个雕花尖。

normal.en: Pin-na-CLE: the last syllable is the little peak itself.
normal.cn: pin-na-CLE：最后一个音节就是那个小峰。

normal.en: Say PIN-uh-kl; the first syllable is as short as the point is thin.
normal.cn: 读成 PIN-uh-kl，第一音节短得像那个尖一样细。

normal.en: Pair it with career: a career is a mountain that the word lets you climb.
normal.cn: 把它和 career 配对：事业是一座由这个词允许你攀爬的山。

abstract.en: A pinnacle is always relative: remove the mountain and the point is only a stone.
abstract.cn: 顶点总是相对的：抽掉那座山，尖也只是一块石头。

abstract.en: The word suits both buildings and lives because both are judged by their highest part.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时适合建筑与人生，因为两者都按最高处被评判。

abstract.en: Every pinnacle implies a slope behind it, which is why the word often carries a warning.
abstract.cn: 每个顶点都暗示身后有一段坡，所以这个词常带警告。

examples.en: Everyone said he had reached the pinnacle of the firm.
examples.cn: 人人都说他已经到了公司的顶峰。

examples.en: That quartet remains the pinnacle of his chamber music.
examples.cn: 那首四重奏至今仍是他室内乐的顶点。

examples.en: He held the board on the pinnacle for a full second.
examples.cn: 他在浪尖上把板稳住了整整一秒。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses climb one shape: an ornament on a roof, a rock, a career, a work of art, a style, a social rank, the top of a road and the crest of a wave.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在攀爬同一个形状：屋顶上的饰物、岩石、事业、艺术作品、风格、社会等级、路的最高处与浪尖。

intro.en: The pinna family is about feathers and points: a pinnate leaf is feather-shaped, and a pinnacle is the point a feather makes in stone.
intro.cn: pinna 词族关乎羽毛与尖：pinnate 的叶子是羽状的，而 pinnacle 是羽毛在石头里留下的那个尖。

latinIntro.en: Latin pinna gives the feather, pinnaculum gives the small point, and English keeps both the roof sense and the height sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pinna 给出羽毛，pinnaculum 给出小尖；英语把屋顶义与高度义都留了下来。
